objects.description: Concrete request class that is both a SubTask and a CommSession. It encapsulates scheduling and execution of a communication request via a CommScheduler for a given CommSchedObject, tracking state, error, timeout reason, and the resulting CommTarget. Provides getters/setters for the request object and wait timeout, and a dispatch() method that submits the request to the scheduler and handles errors. The handle() method is a protected virtual callback invoked to process completion/error; its implementation is not shown here.

Abstract base class for schedulable communication objects that expose load metrics and an acquire(wait_timeout) method used by CommScheduler to obtain a CommTarget for making a request. Holds max_load and cur_load. Details of load semantics are not documented here.

A schedulable group of CommSchedTarget instances that maintains a heap of targets and selects one via acquire(wait_timeout). Provides init/deinit and add/remove management. Uses mutex/cond for synchronization.

A schedulable client-side communication target that is also a CommTarget. Initialized with socket address, timeouts, and max concurrent connections; optional SSL context variant calls set_ssl. Implements acquire(wait_timeout) to obtain capacity and release() to return it. Thread-safe via mutex/cond and participates in a CommSchedGroup.

High-level scheduler that wraps a Communicator. It acquires a CommTarget from a CommSchedObject with an optional wait timeout, then issues requests. Also forwards service, IO, and sleep operations to the underlying Communicator. Lifecycle managed via init/deinit.

Abstract base representing a transport connection. Provides a virtual destructor; concrete subclasses may wrap sockets/SSL state. No constructors provided here; typically created by CommTarget/CommService via new_connection().

Represents a client-side endpoint/target, managing address, timeouts, optional SSL, and an idle connection list. Can be subclassed to customize socket creation, connection object allocation, and SSL init. Must be initialized via init() and deinitialized via deinit().
Abstract outgoing message. Subclasses implement encode() to provide iovecs for transmission.
Abstract incoming message, privately deriving from poller_message_t. Subclasses implement append() to consume bytes; may provide feedback packets and adjust timing via renew().

Abstract session representing a single request/reply exchange or service interaction. Subclasses supply message_in/out and handle lifecycle callbacks and timeouts. Communicator drives it. Holds pointers to target/connection/messages and sequence metadata.

Abstract server-side service bound to an address. Manages listening, SSL accept, session creation via new_session(), and lifecycle callbacks. Must be initialized via init() and later deinitialized. Maintains keep-alive connections.
Abstract timer-based session used for sleeping/delays. Implement duration() to specify timeout; handle() receives completion/error. Internals managed by Communicator.
Custom event handler interface for scheduling and waiting on routines, used by Communicator to integrate with external event loops/threads.

Central orchestrator managing pollers, handler threads, IO services, and lifecycle of sessions/services. Provides APIs to request/reply, bind/unbind services, sleep scheduling, and integration with IOService and custom event handlers.

Concrete task class that requests a sleep operation from a Communicator/CommScheduler. It derives from SubTask and SleepSession (both defined elsewhere) to integrate with the workflow task system and the scheduler’s sleep facility. It stores the resulting state and error, and marks the subtask done when the sleep completes or fails. Construction requires a CommScheduler pointer; lifetime and destruction rules are not stated in this header. Cancellation delegates to scheduler->unsleep(this).

Concrete request task that is both a SubTask and an ExecSession. It represents a unit of work submitted to an Executor via an ExecQueue. dispatch() asks the associated Executor to process the request; on failure it calls handle(ES_STATE_ERROR, errno). The class keeps the processing state and error code, and signals completion via subtask_done() in handle(). Lifetime/ownership: holds raw pointers to an ExecQueue and an Executor, which are expected to outlive the ExecRequest or be managed externally. Details of ES_STATE_ERROR, SubTask, ExecSession, ExecQueue, and Executor are declared elsewhere and not defined in this header.

Concrete request object that participates in the workflow task system (SubTask) and acts as an IO session (IOSession). It is constructed with an IOService pointer and, when dispatched, asks the service to issue the request; on failure it records IOS state/error and completes the subtask. The class stores the last I/O state and errno, and calls subtask_done() when the request finishes or errors. Exact semantics of IOSession/IOService and the values of IOS_STATE_ERROR are defined elsewhere.

Execution queue that holds pending ExecSession objects. Internally maintains a list_head session_list and a pthread mutex for synchronization. Lifecycle is controlled via init()/deinit(); Executor is declared as a friend to access internals. Actual enqueueing is handled by Executor; direct API for pushing sessions is not exposed here.

Abstract unit of work executed by Executor. Subclasses must implement execute() to perform work and handle(int state, int error) to process completion states ES_STATE_FINISHED/ERROR/CANCELED and an error code. Each session is associated with an ExecQueue accessible via get_queue(). Executor is a friend and manages execution and state transitions.

Thread-pool based executor that runs ExecSession tasks. Provides init/deinit to manage a thread pool of nthreads, request() to submit a session to a target ExecQueue, and methods to increase/decrease thread count. Internally uses an opaque thrdpool and static helpers for thread routine and task cancellation.

objects.definition:
#define ES_STATE_FINISHED	0
#define ES_STATE_ERROR		1
#define ES_STATE_CANCELED	2
objects.description: Integer constants representing ExecSession completion states: finished (0), error (1), and canceled (2). Used as the 'state' parameter passed to ExecSession::handle().

Doubly linked list node used by the Linux-style circular intrusive list implementation. Each node holds pointers to the previous and next nodes; list heads are self-referential when the list is empty.
Singly linked list node used for an intrusive forward list. Each node points to the next node or NULL at the end.

Singly linked list head/sentinel for the intrusive forward list. Contains a dummy first node whose next points to the first real element (or NULL when empty), and a last pointer to the final real node or to the dummy first when empty.

objects.definition: typedef struct __mpoller mpoller_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle typedef for the multi-thread poller object defined later in this header. Use with the mpoller_* API to create, start, stop, and destroy a multi-threaded poller. It aliases the underlying struct __mpoller.

Concrete definition of the multi-thread poller object. It holds an array buffer (nodes_buf), a thread count (nthreads), and a flexible/variably-sized array of poller_t pointers (poller[1]) for per-thread pollers. Details of nodes_buf usage are not documented here. Construction and lifecycle are managed through the mpoller_* API in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct __poller poller_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to the poller instance. The underlying struct __poller is not defined in this header, making this an incomplete type used as a handle for creating, starting, modifying, stopping, and destroying a poller.

Message buffer object used by the poller to accumulate or serialize I/O payloads. It provides an append callback to add data and a flexible trailing storage area (zero-length array) for variable-sized data appended after the header. The concrete allocation and lifecycle are managed by the poller or user callbacks via create_message.

Input descriptor for a single poller operation. The operation field selects the I/O or timer action (read, write, listen, connect, recvfrom, SSL variants, event, notify). Depending on operation, the appropriate union member must be set: e.g., create_message for read/recv; partial_written and write_iov/iovcnt for write; accept for listen; recvfrom for UDP; event/notify for custom events. fd is the target file descriptor; ssl may be set for SSL operations. context is user data passed to callbacks. The trailing union carries either an input message buffer for reads, an iovec array for writes, or a generic result pointer used by certain operations.

Output/result object delivered to the user-provided callback when an operation completes, changes, or fails. state indicates completion status; error holds errno-style error code when applicable; data echoes the associated poller_data along with operation-specific results (e.g., message filled, result pointers).
Configuration for creating a poller. Sets resource limits, the central completion callback receiving poller_result and user context pointer, and the callback context itself. Passed to poller_create.

objects.definition: typedef struct __msgqueue msgqueue_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a simple message queue. The underlying struct __msgqueue is intentionally not defined in this header, making the type opaque to users. The queue supports blocking/nonblocking modes and can hold messages whose node link is located at a byte offset 'linkoff' from the message head, where at least pointer-sized space must be available for internal linkage. Max pending messages may reach up to twice 'maxlen' in blocking mode and is unbounded in nonblocking mode. Details of internal fields and memory ownership are not exposed here.

Intrusive red-black tree node storing links to parent, left, right, and a 1-byte color (RB_RED/RB_BLACK). Nodes are intended to be embedded within user structs to participate in an rbtree. Packed to 1-byte alignment due to #pragma pack(1). Color must be initialized to red when linking. Destruction is by removing from the tree (rb_erase).
Red-black tree root container holding a pointer to the root rb_node. Use RB_ROOT macro for static initialization to NULL root. The root owns the tree of rb_node elements.

Abstract base class representing a unit of work to be dispatched. Users implement dispatch() to perform work and typically call subtask_done() when finished. It maintains a pointer to an owning ParallelTask (parent) and a generic user pointer for associating arbitrary data. The done() method is a private pure-virtual hook used by the framework to chain completion; not directly callable by users. Construction is default; destruction is virtual. Ownership: may be managed by ParallelTask via the private parent field.

Concrete SubTask that coordinates a set of SubTask instances to run in parallel. Holds an array of SubTask pointers and the count (subtasks_nr); internally tracks remaining subtasks via nleft. The dispatch() method initiates the parallel execution (implementation not shown here). It does not allocate the subtasks; the caller provides the array and count. It owns/coordinates the supplied SubTask objects during execution but lifetime management details are not specified in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct __thrdpool thrdpool_t;
objects.description: Opaque thread-pool handle. The concrete struct __thrdpool is intentionally not defined in this header, making thrdpool_t an incomplete type used to refer to a thread pool instance managed by the library. Details of its fields and lifecycle are hidden; users operate on it via the provided API.
Task descriptor submitted to a thread pool. It holds a work routine taking a single void* argument and the corresponding context pointer passed to that routine.

Abstract base class representing a single asynchronous I/O session. Subclasses implement prepare() to set up one I/O operation using the protected prep_* helpers, and handle(state,error) to consume completion results. Internally stores an iocb buffer and result value and is linked via list_head for service management. Destruction is virtual. Details of prep_* semantics are not present here; they likely prepare Linux AIO control blocks. get_res() returns the operation result after completion.

Service class managing Linux AIO-based sessions. init(maxevents) initializes internal resources (eventfd, io_context), deinit() tears them down. request(session) submits an IOSession for asynchronous processing. Provides virtual hooks handle_stop() and handle_unbound() for lifecycle events; subclasses must implement handle_unbound(). Thread-safety via mutex; maintains a session list and reference counting. Uses an eventfd created via create_event_fd().
Incomplete type referenced from list.h representing an intrusive list node used to link IOSession and IOService internal lists. Definition is not present in this header.
Opaque Linux AIO context type referenced as a pointer within IOService. The full definition is not provided here.

Base interface for protocol messages used by the Communicator framework. It inherits from CommMessageOut and CommMessageIn and defines the encode() and append() interfaces for serializing and parsing protocol data. It manages a size limit and an optional Attachment object with ownership semantics (deleted in the destructor). It supports being wrapped by a ProtocolWrapper to delegate feedback/renew behaviors. Construction is default; move construction/assignment transfer the attachment and reset wrapper linkage. Details of CommMessageIn/Out are external to this header.

Opaque extension hook associated with a ProtocolMessage. Intended for user-defined payload or metadata attached to a message. ProtocolMessage owns the Attachment pointer when set and deletes it in its destructor. Only a virtual destructor is defined; no interface is specified here.

A decorator that wraps a ProtocolMessage to intercept/delegate behavior. It forwards encode() and append() to the wrapped message, and inner() returns the innermost message. set_message() links the wrapped message back to this wrapper via its private wrapper pointer. Move operations transfer the wrapped message and maintain linkage. It does not own construction of the wrapped message in this header; ownership semantics are not explicitly documented.

HTTP message parser state object. Holds parsing state, accumulated headers (via list_head), message buffers, and flags for request/response, chunking, keep-alive, etc. Used with http_parser_* APIs to parse or build HTTP messages. Caller must init with http_parser_init and deinit with http_parser_deinit; http_parser_close_message can mark completion. Ownership: header_list nodes are managed internally; external code iterates via cursor APIs.

Iterator/cursor for traversing or manipulating the parser's header list. Initialize with http_header_cursor_init, advance/find/erase with http_header_cursor_next/http_header_cursor_find/http_header_cursor_erase, and rewind with http_header_cursor_rewind. No dynamic resources; deinit is a no-op.

Plain-old-data header field container used to pass an HTTP header name/value pair with explicit lengths to the parser. Names and values are non-owning pointers; lifetimes must outlive use by the parser call. No constructors or methods; stack- or heap-allocatable.

Base HTTP protocol message class providing header management, version handling, body buffering for output, and integration with an internal http_parser_t. Owns an http_parser_t instance and an internal list-based buffer for output body blocks. Users can build/modify messages and query parsing state. Construction requires specifying whether it is a response; destructor clears output body and deinitializes the parser.
HTTP request message class extending HttpMessage with request-specific fields: method and request URI accessors/mutators. Default constructor initializes as a non-response message (request).

HTTP response message class extending HttpMessage with status code and reason phrase accessors/mutators. Default constructor initializes as a response; parse_zero_body() marks a zero-length body (e.g., HEAD).

Represents a single HTTP chunk for chunked transfer encoding. Manages a buffer for chunk payload and encodes/decodes chunk lines. Destructor frees owned chunk_data. Provides methods to get, move (transfer ownership), and set chunk data.

objects.description: Anonymous enumeration that defines a comprehensive set of HTTP status code named constants. As an anonymous enum, no named type is introduced; the constants have type int. Use these integral constants directly; there is no enum type to take the address of. Pointer type is represented here as int* to satisfy the schema, but taking a pointer to an enum constant is not valid C++.

Redis reply node matching hiredis redisReply layout. Represents a single RESP value: string, status, error, integer, nil, or array. Arrays own a vector of child reply pointers. Initialized to NIL via redis_reply_init; content is set via setters. Must be deinitialized with redis_reply_deinit to free any allocated children/strings if applicable.

Stateful Redis RESP parser context. Accumulates incoming bytes and produces a top-level redis_reply_t in the reply field. Holds internal buffers, indices, and a list of read segments. Must be initialized with redis_parser_init and cleaned up with redis_parser_deinit. Use redis_parser_append_message to feed data.

A variant-like container for Redis replies (nil, integer, string/status/error, array). Manages internal storage via a type tag and a void* pointing to allocated data (e.g., std::string, int64_t, std::vector<RedisValue>). Provides setters from C++ values and from a C-style redis_reply_t, accessors, and conversion utilities. Memory management details for free_data/only_set_string_data are defined in the implementation and not shown here.

Base class for Redis protocol messages built atop ProtocolMessage. Holds a redis_parser_t for parsing/encoding, provides encode/append hooks, and flags like asking_. Also exposes parse_success and encode_reply. Implementation details are in the source.

Represents a Redis request message. Provides high-level API to set a command and parameters, and to retrieve them. Overrides encode/append to emit the request over the protocol. Stores user_request_ for later encoding.

Represents a Redis response message. Allows clients to extract the result as a RedisValue or access the underlying redis_reply_t memory via result_ptr for zero-copy C-style interaction. Also allows servers to set a result for encoding. Holds an internal RedisValue for owned/copy-based operations.

MySQL packetization stream context. Manages framing for MySQL protocol packets, tracking header bytes, sequence ID, payload length/remaining, and an internal buffer. Contains a function pointer write to emit data respecting MySQL packet boundaries. Used with mysql_stream_init, mysql_stream_write, mysql_stream_get_seq, mysql_stream_get_buf, and mysql_stream_deinit.

Base protocol message for MySQL protocol handling in the protocol namespace. Provides parsing/encoding append hooks, sequence ID and command accessors, and holds internal state such as mysql_stream_t/mysql_parser_t pointers, packet headers buffer, sequence id, and an internal buffer. Construction/destruction behavior is declared, with move semantics supported. Detailed behavior is defined elsewhere (inlined or source).

Represents a MySQL request message. Provides setters to assign the SQL query and getters to retrieve it or check if it was set. Inherits the encoding/append machinery from MySQLMessage. Defaulted move operations; no explicit resource ownership beyond base class.

Represents a MySQL response message. Can distinguish OK and ERROR packets, expose packet type, and provide metadata such as affected rows, last insert id, warnings, error code/message, SQL state, and info. Supports constructing an OK packet. Overrides decode_packet to parse response payload. Move semantics are defaulted.

Represents a single MySQL result cell with type info and value accessors. Supports type checks, conversions to common C++ types, and zero-copy retrieval of underlying buffer. Storage and lifetime management details are not visible here; implementations are likely in MySQLResult.inl. Exact ownership of data pointer is unknown from this header.

Metadata for a MySQL column within a result set. Provides accessors for names, table/db, default, charset, flags, length/decimals, and type. Internally stores string pointers and lengths parsed from protocol buffers.

Cursor/iterator over MySQLResponse result sets. Supports multiple result sets, field metadata retrieval, row fetching into various containers, zero-copy row access, and statistics like affected rows and insert id. Manages parser/cursor state for streaming through the protocol buffers.

Utility class in the protocol namespace providing static helper functions for escaping MySQL strings. It is not intended to be instantiated (no data members, only static methods). Details of escaping behavior are not provided in this header.

Column/field metadata for a MySQL result set, stored as offsets and lengths into an external buffer. Holds names, table/db info, type, charset, size, flags, and decimals. The struct does not own memory; offsets point into the parser buffer.

Represents a single MySQL result set or OK/ERR packet details. Contains a list node for chaining, server status, counts, row data range as buffer offsets, an array of field descriptors, and OK-packet metadata like affected_rows, insert_id, warnings, and info text location.
Iterator cursor over the parser's internal result_set_list. Maintains head and current list positions for sequential traversal.

Stateful MySQL protocol parser that consumes buffers and builds a list of result sets. Tracks command, packet type, parsing function, buffer base, error info, local infile details, and result set collection and progress. Memory for strings/rows is referenced by offsets into buf; lifecycle managed by init/deinit.

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file contains only inline byte-order utility functions and two C-linkage function declarations for decoding MySQL-length-encoded integers and strings.

A protocol::ProtocolWrapper subclass that provides package-level framing for ProtocolMessage objects. It overrides encode and append to implement message packaging; next_in and next_out are disabled here (return NULL), indicating no wrapper chaining. Move construction/assignment are enabled; copy operations are implicitly disabled. Exact encoding/append semantics are not specified in this header and depend on the implementation in the corresponding source file. Requires ProtocolMessage and ProtocolWrapper from ProtocolMessage.h.

ProtocolMessage-derived helper that performs SSL/TLS handshake framing/parsing on top of OpenSSL. Holds a raw SSL* (not owned here unless documented elsewhere). Provides encode/append to drive handshake I/O. Construction requires an existing SSL*. Ownership and lifecycle of SSL* are unspecified here.

ProtocolWrapper for encrypting/decrypting message streams with OpenSSL. Wraps a ProtocolMessage and an existing SSL* to perform SSL/TLS record I/O via encode/append and feedback. Raw SSL* is stored; ownership is not specified in this header. append_message is an internal helper.

Server-side specialization of SSLWrapper that customizes append behavior for server SSL/TLS processing. Requires a ProtocolMessage and an SSL* already configured for server use. SSL* ownership/lifecycle are unspecified here.
OpenSSL SSL session/context handle used by the wrappers. Declared in <openssl/ssl.h>; not defined here. Included to clarify pointer fields used within classes.
Packed DNS message header with ID, flags (bitfields with endianness handling), and section counts. Represents on-the-wire layout without byte-order conversion.
DNS question section entry: name, type, and class. Stores decoded qname string pointer.
RDATA structure for SOA records: primary name server, responsible mailbox, and zone timers/counters.
RDATA structure for SRV records containing priority, weight, port, and target host.
RDATA structure for MX records holding preference and exchange hostname.

Generic DNS resource record node containing owner name, type/class, TTL, RDATA length, and a pointer to type-specific RDATA (e.g., raw bytes, SOA/SRV/MX structs, or strings). Intended for linkage in lists.

Stateful DNS message builder/parser. Holds buffers, parse cursor, completion flags, header/question, and three record lists (answer/authority/additional). Lifecycle managed by dns_parser_init/deinit; content appended via dns_parser_append_message and populated by dns_parser_set_* or parsed by dns_parser_parse_all.

Iterator over a list of dns_record entries. Use dns_answer_cursor_init/dns_authority_cursor_init/dns_additional_cursor_init to bind to a section, iterate with dns_record_cursor_next, and deinit is a no-op.

Base DNS protocol message class that wraps a dns_parser_t and exposes getters/setters for DNS header, question, and methods to add resource records. It owns a dns_parser_t pointer and message buffer, and implements encoding/append hooks for ProtocolMessage. Construction allocates and initializes the parser; destruction deinitializes and deletes it. Move operations are declared. Details of encode/append behavior are defined in the implementation file.
Derived request message for DNS queries. Provides a convenience set_question() to initialize the question section in the underlying parser. Uses DnsMessage’s construction and ownership model.

Derived DNS message for responses. Tracks the associated request ID and request name for matching/validation. Overrides append to handle streaming/assembly specifics. It does not change ownership of the parser from DnsMessage.

Opaque DNS parser struct referenced via pointer by DnsMessage. Not defined in this header; definition resides in dns_parser.h. Used to hold DNS header, question, and resource records, and to encode/decode messages. Details unknown in this file.

Utility class providing static helpers to convert a DnsResponse into addrinfo structures and to free them. Construction is not intended; only static methods are exposed. Details of allocation strategy and ownership are not documented here; callers should assume the returned addrinfo chain must be freed via DnsUtil::freeaddrinfo.

Cursor-style iterator over DNS sections (answer, authority, additional) for a given DnsResponse. It wraps an internal dns_record_cursor_t and parser obtained from the response. Provides methods to reset which section is being iterated, advance to the next record, and search for a CNAME. Move operations are disabled; lifetime is tied to the underlying DnsResponse/parser, which must outlive the cursor.

A ProtocolMessage-derived class implementing a simple TLV (Type-Length-Value) message. It stores an integer type and a std::string payload. It maintains a two-word header (likely type and length) and tracks how many header bytes have been received during parsing. Encoding fills iovec vectors; append consumes input bytes to parse/assemble the message. Exact wire format/semantics beyond TLV are inferred and not fully documented here.

Public configuration and data models for Consul protocol usage. ConsulConfig is a reference-counted handle class that wraps an internal Config with health check options. Also defines ConsulAddress alias and service-related structs for discovery/registration payloads.

objects.definition: using ConsulAddress = std::pair<std::string, unsigned short>;
objects.description: Alias for an address and port pair. Represents network endpoints for Consul services.
Describes a Consul service registration, including identifiers, tags, multiple network addresses and metadata.
Aggregates node information, an embedded ConsulService, and health-check fields to represent a discovered service instance.
Simple mapping of a service name to a list of tags used for filtering or categorization.

Configuration struct for WFServerBase/WFServer instances. Controls transport type, connection limits, timeouts, request size limit, and SSL accept timeout. Details such as TransportType enum values are defined elsewhere.

Abstract base class for network servers. Provides start/serve APIs for TCP/SSL, lifecycle control (shutdown/stop/wait_finish), connection counting, and SSL context hooks. Inherits from CommService (defined elsewhere). Must be subclassed or used via the WFServer template for concrete request/response handling.

objects.definition: using dns_process_t = std::function<void (WFDnsTask *)>;
objects.description: Alias for a callable that processes a DNS task: a function or functor taking a WFDnsTask* and returning void. Used by the DNS server to handle incoming DNS requests. Destruction/ownership follows std::function semantics; the pointed-to WFDnsTask is managed by the framework.

objects.definition:
using WFDnsServer = WFServer<protocol::DnsRequest,
							 protocol::DnsResponse>;
objects.description: Type alias for a workflow server specialized for DNS, handling protocol::DnsRequest and protocol::DnsResponse. Construction is provided via a template specialization of WFServer constructor that accepts a dns_process_t. Lifecycle is managed as a WFServer; this alias itself introduces no new members beyond the specialized constructor provided inline in this header.

A constexpr instance of WFServerParams providing default parameters for a DNS server (UDP transport, connection/timeouts, size limits). Concrete task class derived from WFGenericTask that wraps a WFHttpTask to process HTTP chunked transfer responses incrementally. Exposes accessors to the underlying request/response, per-chunk timeouts, SSL context forwarding, and user-supplied extract and callback handlers invoked per chunk or at completion. A connection helper class for creating workflow MySQL tasks bound to a specific MySQL endpoint (ParsedURI) and optional OpenSSL SSL_CTX. It wraps initialization from a MySQL URL, applies an SSL context to created WFMySQLTask instances, provides creation of query tasks and a disconnect task, and tracks a user-provided connection id to distinguish concurrent connections. Destruction does not actively close the TCP connection unless create_disconnect_task is used; connections may be kept alive and reused by other WFMySQLConnection instances with the same id and URL.

Active object representing a Redis pub/sub subscription task integrated with the workflow framework. Provides synchronous send helpers (subscribe/unsubscribe/psubscribe/punsubscribe/ping/quit), timeout tuning, and supports user-provided extract and callback handlers. Lifetime is manually managed via release(); after release(), only use inside extract until callback completes. Internally wraps a WFRedisTask and participates in a series via WFGenericTask.

Factory/owner for creating Redis subscription tasks bound to a specific Redis URI and optional OpenSSL SSL_CTX. Provides init() to parse URL and set TLS context, and helpers to create subscribe/psubscribe tasks with user extract and callback handlers. Manages SSL context assignment on created tasks.

DNS client class that manages configuration (resolver URL and optional search parameters) and creates DNS tasks. Holds internal parameters pointer and an atomic identifier. Destructor is virtual. Cache entry holding a resolved addrinfo plus timing metadata. Fields: addrinfo (owned per flags), confident_time (when the result became confident), expire_time (absolute expiry). delayed() checks whether the addrinfo is marked as delayed (bit 1<<1 set in ai_flags). Value lifetimes are managed by DnsCache via ValueDeleter; callers should not free addrinfo directly.

Thread-safe DNS result cache with RAII-like handles. Provides get/get_ttl/get_confident to acquire a const DnsHandle to a cached DnsCacheValue, put to insert entries with TTL policy, release to return a handle, and del to remove a key. Users must call release on handles obtained from get/put. Internally uses LRUCache with ValueDeleter to free underlying addrinfo: if ai_flags bit 0 is set, uses freeaddrinfo; otherwise uses protocol::DnsUtil::freeaddrinfo. Construction and destruction semantics depend on LRUCache; this header declares a public ctor/dtor.

Global configuration record for the Workflow library. Holds endpoint parameters, DNS behavior, thread counts for various pools, event limits, and resolver file paths. Values are applied process-wide via WORKFLOW_library_init or WFGlobal::set_global_settings.

Callback/function type used to supply routing logic for consistent-hash and manual selection modes. It is only referenced here; the actual typedef definition is not present in this header. The docs imply the callable maps URI components (path, query, fragment) to a non-negative 32-bit integer; exact signature is defined elsewhere.

Top-level manager for routing/scheduling connections. Owns a cache (rb_root) and mutex, provides get() to obtain routing info and static notifications to update availability. Lightweight result container used with RouteManager::get(). Holds an opaque cookie and a request_object pointer for the scheduler. Provides default initialization and a clear() helper. Lifetime and ownership of cookie/request_object are external/unknown in this header.

A concrete scheduling target derived from CommSchedTarget. Wraps init/deinit to manage SSL_CTX refcount and exposes a state field. Overrides new_connection to create WFConnection instances. Lifecycle aligned with CommSchedTarget; deinit must be called to release SSL_CTX.
Enumeration of transport protocols a client task may use, including plain TCP/UDP/SCTP and their TLS/SSL variants for TCP and SCTP.
Configuration struct for client networking behavior: address family, connection concurrency limit, connect/response/SSL connect timeouts (milliseconds), and whether to use TLS SNI.
A constexpr instance providing default values for EndpointParams. Not a new type; listed as an alias to highlight the provided canonical default instance defined in this header.

Primary facilities class providing utility helpers: sleep/asynchronous sleep, task submission (go), network request helpers (templated), and asynchronous file I/O wrappers returning WFFuture. It also declares an inner WaitGroup class and several internal callbacks. Implementations are not present here.

Inner synchronization helper similar to Go's WaitGroup. Manages a counter of outstanding tasks; wait methods block (or wait with timeout) until the count reaches zero. Uses an internal WFCounterTask and WFFuture to signal completion. Construction takes initial count; add/done adjust it. Destruction semantics are not detailed here.

An encoder helper class that accumulates byte ranges into an iovec array and an internal buffer list for protocol message encoding. It supports zero-copy appends of existing memory (append_nocopy) and copy-based appends (append_copy). The stream tracks the number of iovec entries (size_) and total bytes (bytes_), can be reset with a new external iovec array, and exposes operator<< helpers for common inputs. Internal methods merge() and clear_buf_data() are declared but defined elsewhere. Ownership details: it references an external iovec array provided by the user and manages an internal buffer list (buf_list_) whose lifetime is handled by clear_buf_data().

Static-only utility class providing common string helpers: URL decoding in-place, URL encoding (full and component/segment), splitting by a separator (optionally filtering empty tokens), trimming/stripping, and prefix checking. No instances are required or implied; all methods are static. Ownership and lifetime are irrelevant since there is no state.

RAII wrapper holding parsed components of a URI. Owns C-string buffers for each component and tracks parse state and error code. Copy and move semantics are declared; copy performs deep copy via copy(), and move operations are declared but defined elsewhere. init() zeroes fields; deinit() frees all component buffers. Users should rely on URIParser::parse to populate fields and on destructor to free them.

Static utility class providing URI parsing and helpers. parse() fills a ParsedURI (0 on success, -1 on failure). split_query_strict parses a query string into possibly multi-valued map, split_query into single-valued map, and split_path splits a path into segments. No instances are intended (all-static).

objects.description: Anonymous enumeration of workflow task state codes. Provides symbolic constants representing task lifecycle and error states used across tasks in this header. Backed by external communicator state macros for some values.
Timer-based task built on SleepRequest. Runs a callback upon completion and self-destructs. Holds user_data and exposes state/error accessors.
Simple generic task derived from SubTask that immediately completes on dispatch. Holds user_data and explicit state/error members. Serves as a base for several synchronization/utility tasks below.
Counter-based synchronization task. Each count() decrements an atomic counter; when it reaches zero, marks success and completes. Supports a completion callback and self-destruction.

Mailbox synchronization task. Exposes a void* mailbox slot; send(msg) stores message and completes when both sender and receiver rendezvous (flag toggled twice). Supports optional external mailbox pointer or internal user_data backing.

Selector task that races multiple candidates. submit(msg) attempts to set the winning message once; when any submit succeeds and the receiver has arrived, completes with success. If all candidates finish without a message, completes with ENOMSG system error.
Conditional task that defers execution of a provided SubTask until either dispatch occurs or an external signal(msg) arrives. Stores message into msgbuf and completes when both sides rendezvous.
Lightweight task executed on an Executor via ExecRequest, mainly used to run a function asynchronously and invoke a completion callback. Self-destructs on completion.
Repeating task that repeatedly generates and schedules a new SubTask using a provided factory until it returns null, then completes with success. Supports final callback.

Composite module task combining ParallelTask and an embedded SeriesWork to run a sub-graph starting at 'first'. Exposes a sub_series for building internal sequences, supports a completion callback, and self-cleans unfinished graphs on destruction.

Graph node used within WFGraphTask to build a dependency graph of tasks. Inherits WFCounterTask (protected), maintaining a list of successor nodes and a counter (via WFCounterTask) that is incremented when setting precedence. Methods let you declare edges: precede() adds an edge from this to another; succeed() adds the reverse. Overloaded operators provide syntactic sugar for establishing edges. The actual execution behavior and completion handling are performed in the overridden done() (defined elsewhere). Construction is protected; nodes are created by WFGraphTask. Destruction is virtual.

A task that manages and executes a graph of SubTask nodes. Provides factory create_graph_node() to allocate WFGraphNode objects bound to underlying SubTask operations, and supports an optional completion callback via set_callback(). On construction it creates an internal ParallelWork via Workflow::create_parallel_work to help scheduling. Execution lifecycle is implemented in dispatch() and done() (defined elsewhere).

A resource pool managing a fixed array of void* resources with blocking/conditional get and post operations integrated with the workflow task system. It exposes get() to acquire a resource (optionally returning it via resbuf) associated with a SubTask, and post() to return a resource. Internally it maintains a Data struct with the resource array, an index acting as a stack pointer, a wait list for blocked requests, and a mutex for synchronization. pop/push are virtual to allow customization of allocation/return strategy over the underlying array. Construction can be with an existing array of resources or by specifying a capacity to be created internally. Destruction deletes the internally managed res array. Details about get/post semantics and thread-safety beyond the mutex are not documented here.

Inner helper struct storing the resource pool state and providing thin wrappers that delegate to the owning WFResourcePool's virtual pop/push. Fields: res is the array of resource pointers; index tracks the current position for push/pop; wait_list holds pending acquisitions (type list_head is external); mutex guards concurrent access; value likely holds the current available count or a flag (not fully documented); pool points back to the owning WFResourcePool.

A message queue class that provides posting and retrieval of opaque messages (void*) with task-aware waiting via WFConditional and SubTask. It manages two intrusive lists (message list and waiters list) protected by a mutex. Messages are stored internally as MessageEntry nodes in msg_list. Data is an embedded helper/handle allowing external code to call back into the owning queue's push/pop through a stored pointer. Exact synchronization and wake-up semantics are defined in the corresponding implementation, not shown here.

Helper struct embedded in WFMessageQueue that holds the queue state: intrusive lists for messages and waiters, a mutex for synchronization, and a back-pointer to the owning WFMessageQueue. Provides thin wrappers redirecting push/pop to the owning queue. Construction initializes lists and queue pointer in WFMessageQueue's constructor.

Concrete task type deriving from WFGenericTask that represents a router task in the name service. It stores a RouteResult produced by routing and invokes a user-provided callback in done(), then self-destructs and advances the series. set_state and set_error delegate to the WFGenericTask base (not shown here).
Tracing/attachment container for name-service operations. Holds arbitrary user data and an optional deleter callback for cleanup. No ownership semantics beyond the deleter pointer are defined here.

Parameter bundle passed to name-service policy to construct routing tasks. Includes transport type, target URI reference, optional info string, SSL context, flags for fixed address/connection, retry count, and optional tracing object. Several member types are declared elsewhere and are only referenced here.

Abstract policy interface for name resolution and routing. Implementations must create router tasks given WFNSParams and may override success/failed hooks to update availability. Provides default implementations that notify RouteManager. Destructor is virtual.

Registry/manager for WFNSPolicy instances keyed by name, with a configurable default policy. Internally stores policies in an rbtree protected by a pthread rwlock. Provides add/get/del functions. get_policy_entry and WFNSPolicyEntry are declared but defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: using router_callback_t = std::function<void (WFRouterTask *)>;
objects.description: Type alias for the callback invoked by WFRouterTask upon completion. It receives the WFRouterTask pointer.

A router task implementation that resolves hostnames to endpoints using DNS and WFNS policy parameters. It stores name-service parameters, endpoint parameters, DNS TTL defaults/minima, and manages asynchronous DNS callbacks and task lifecycle. Construction requires WFNSParams and a router callback; an overload also accepts EndpointParams and TTL settings.

A name-service policy that produces WFRouterTask instances for DNS resolution. It implements create_router_task to build router tasks based on WFNSParams. Details of construction logic are defined in the implementation file.

objects.definition:
struct AddressParams
{
	struct EndpointParams endpoint_params; ///< Connection config
	unsigned int dns_ttl_default;          ///< in seconds, DNS TTL when network request success
	unsigned int dns_ttl_min;              ///< in seconds, DNS TTL when network request fail
/**
 * - The max_fails directive sets the number of consecutive unsuccessful attempts to communicate with the server.
 * - After 30s following the server failure, upstream probe the server with some live client`s requests.
 * - If the probes have been successful, the server is marked as a live one.
 * - If max_fails is set to 1, it means server would out of upstream selection in 30 seconds when failed only once
 */
	unsigned int max_fails;                ///< [1, INT32_MAX] max_fails = 0 means max_fails = 1
	unsigned short weight;                 ///< [1, 65535] weight = 0 means weight = 1. only for main server
	int server_type;                       ///< 0 for main and 1 for backup
	int group_id;                          ///< -1 means no group. Backup without group will be backup for any main
};
objects.description: Configuration for a server/address instance used by service governance. Includes endpoint connection parameters, DNS TTLs, failure threshold, weight, and grouping/role (main or backup).
Internal policy-ready copy of AddressParams containing only fields relevant to runtime selection and DNS behavior. Constructible empty or from AddressParams.
Represents a single backend endpoint with parsed host/port, failure tracking, breaker timeout, and per-endpoint policy parameters. Contains an embedded list node for breaker management.

A name-service policy implementing service governance: server pool management, selection strategies, circuit-breaker behavior, and lifecycle hooks for routing success/failure. Manages EndpointAddress instances and exposes APIs to add/replace/remove/enable/disable servers and query current addresses.
Embedded node to link an EndpointAddress into breaker_list via list_head. Holds back-pointer to the owning EndpointAddress.
Alias for a callable taking URI path, query, and fragment C-strings and returning an unsigned int used as a routing/hash selector. Pointer form is upstream_route_t *.

Address parameter wrapper extending PolicyAddrParams with upstream-specific fields: weight, server_type, group_id, and owning EndpointGroup pointer. Provides a constructor from AddressParams and an address string. Exact semantics depend on external base/related types.

Base governance policy for upstream endpoint groups. Manages groups and selection, server add/replace/remove, liveness/fusing/recovery, and a hash map of addresses. Owns a group map and a default EndpointGroup pointer. Provides selection entry point and helper methods. Requires external WFServiceGovernance/EndpointAddress semantics.
Round-robin selection policy derived from UPSGroupPolicy. Uses an atomic index to cycle through endpoints. Supports optional try-another fallback strategy and custom removal handling.
Weighted-random selection policy with per-endpoint weights. Tracks total and available weights, custom add/remove, and adjusts on fuse/recover. Offers try-another behavior.
Virtual-node smooth weighted round-robin policy built atop UPSWeightedRandomPolicy. Maintains pre-generated sequences and current weights for smooth distribution; no try-another fallback.
Consistent-hash based selection policy. Accepts a routing function to compute the hash from URI components, and manages add/remove hooks accordingly.
Manual selection policy where callers provide function objects to choose the primary and fallback endpoints based on URI. Supports optional try-another behavior and custom add/remove hooks.

functions.name: CommRequest::dispatch

requirements: scheduler must be a valid, non-null pointer to a functioning CommScheduler instance when dispatch is called.
object should be set appropriately for the scheduler->request call; if null or invalid, behavior is scheduler-defined and may result in an error path.
