requirements: chunk_data must be non-null if size > 0; size may be zero.
Callers must check the boolean return value for success/failure.

functions.name: protocol::HttpMessageChunk::HttpMessageChunk
functions.description: Constructs an empty HTTP chunk message with no chunk data and zero bytes received.
requirements: No special preconditions.

functions.name: protocol::HttpMessageChunk::HttpMessageChunk
functions.description: Move-constructs an HttpMessageChunk, transferring ownership of any internal chunk buffer and state from msg.
requirements: msg becomes a moved-from object and should only be destroyed or assigned to afterward.

functions.name: protocol::HttpMessageChunk::~HttpMessageChunk
functions.description: Destroys the chunk message and frees any owned chunk_data buffer.
requirements: After destruction, any previously moved-out data remains caller-owned; internal pointers become invalid.

functions.name: protocol::HttpMessageChunk::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns an HttpMessageChunk, releasing current resources and taking ownership of msg's chunk buffer and state.
requirements: After assignment, msg is in a valid but unspecified (moved-from) state.

functions.name: protocol::HttpUtil::set_response_status
functions.description: Sets the HTTP status code on an HttpResponse. Typical usage is to specify the numeric HTTP status (e.g., 200, 404) before sending a response. Other details (e.g., reason phrase) are not shown here and may be set implicitly by the implementation.
requirements: resp must be a valid, non-null pointer to an HttpResponse object.
status_code should be a valid HTTP status code integer (e.g., 100–599); behavior for out-of-range values is unspecified.
The HttpResponse object must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: protocol::HttpUtil::decode_chunked_body
functions.description: Decodes a Transfer-Encoding: chunked HTTP message body from the provided HttpMessage and returns the decoded payload as a contiguous string. Use this when the message used chunked transfer encoding and you need the raw body.
requirements: msg must be a valid, non-null pointer to an HttpMessage that contains a parsed HTTP message.
The message should represent a chunked body; behavior for non-chunked bodies is unspecified.
The HttpMessage must remain valid during the call.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderMap::HttpHeaderMap
functions.description: Constructs a header map from the given HttpMessage, likely aggregating header names and their values into an internal unordered_map for convenient lookup. Intended for read-only access patterns over an existing message’s headers.
requirements: message must be a valid, non-null pointer to an HttpMessage with headers already parsed.
The HttpMessage should remain valid at least for the duration of construction; whether the map stores copies or references is unknown.
Header name normalization (e.g., case-insensitivity) is not specified.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderMap::key_exists
functions.description: Checks if a header with the given name exists in the map. Returns true if present.
requirements: key may be any string; matching semantics (case sensitivity, trimming) are unspecified.
The HttpHeaderMap instance must have been constructed successfully.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderMap::get
functions.description: Retrieves a header value by name and returns it as a string. If multiple values exist, the selection policy is unspecified (likely returns the first). If not found, returned value behavior is unspecified (likely empty string).
requirements: key may be any string; matching semantics (case sensitivity, trimming) are unspecified.
Callers should handle the possibility of an empty return when the key is absent.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderMap::get_strict
functions.description: Returns all values for the specified header as a vector of strings, without implicit merging. Useful when headers may appear multiple times.
requirements: key may be any string; matching semantics are unspecified.
If the key is absent, the returned vector may be empty.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::HttpHeaderCursor
functions.description: Initializes a cursor over the headers of the provided HttpMessage, enabling iteration, search, and removal of headers using a low-level parser-backed cursor.
requirements: message must be a valid, non-null pointer to an HttpMessage; message->get_parser() must be valid.
The HttpMessage and its underlying parser must remain valid for the lifetime of the cursor.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::~HttpHeaderCursor
functions.description: Destructor that deinitializes the underlying header cursor resources.
requirements: The associated HttpMessage/parser must not be destroyed before the cursor is destroyed if the cursor still references them.
Must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::next
functions.description: Advances the cursor to the next header and outputs its name and value into the provided HttpMessageHeader structure. Returns true on success, false on end or failure.
requirements: header must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable HttpMessageHeader.
On success, header->name, header->name_len, header->value, and header->value_len are populated by the function.
The cursor must have been initialized with a valid HttpMessage and not be at the end of headers.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::next
functions.description: Advances to the next header and returns its name and value as strings. Returns true on success, false on end or failure. This is a higher-level convenience overload.
requirements: name and value must be valid string references; they will be assigned on success.
The cursor must be initialized and not at end of headers.
Exact formatting/normalization of header names and values is unspecified.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::find
functions.description: Searches for a header matching the name provided in header->name (with header->name_len specifying its length) and outputs its value into the same structure. Returns true on success.
requirements: header must be a valid, non-null pointer to a HttpMessageHeader with header->name and header->name_len initialized to the target name.
On success, header->value and header->value_len are set.
Matching semantics (case sensitivity) are not specified.
The cursor must be associated with a valid HttpMessage.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::find
functions.signature: bool protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::find(const std::string& name, std::string& value);
functions.description: Finds the first header with the specified name and writes its value to the output parameter. Returns true if found.
requirements: name is the target header name; matching semantics (case sensitivity) are unspecified.
value must be a valid reference; it will be assigned on success.
Caller must check the boolean return value to determine success.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::erase
functions.description: Erases the header at the current cursor position. Returns true on success.
requirements: There must be a valid current header selected by a prior successful next() or find(); behavior otherwise is unspecified.
Alters the underlying header list; subsequent cursor state after erase is determined by the underlying parser’s semantics (unspecified here).

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::find_and_erase
functions.description: Finds a header by name using the provided HttpMessageHeader (name fields pre-filled) and erases it if found. Returns true only if the header was found and erased.
requirements: header must be a valid, non-null pointer with header->name and header->name_len initialized.
On success the matching header is removed from the message’s headers.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::find_and_erase
functions.description: Finds a header by name and erases it if present. Returns true on success (found and erased).
requirements: name is the target header name; matching semantics are unspecified.
Modifies the underlying message headers on success.

functions.name: protocol::HttpHeaderCursor::rewind
functions.description: Resets the header cursor to the beginning, allowing iteration from the first header again.
requirements: The cursor must be initialized with a valid HttpMessage.
Existing references obtained from previous iterations may become invalid after modifications; behavior is otherwise unspecified.

functions.name: protocol::HttpChunkCursor::HttpChunkCursor
functions.description: Initializes a cursor for iterating over chunks in an HTTP message body, typically when Transfer-Encoding: chunked is used.
requirements: message must be a valid, non-null pointer to an HttpMessage that contains the body to iterate.
The HttpMessage must remain valid for the lifetime of the cursor.

functions.name: protocol::HttpChunkCursor::~HttpChunkCursor
functions.description: Destructor for the chunk cursor; performs any necessary cleanup. Inline in the header as a no-op.
requirements: Must not be used after destruction.
Underlying HttpMessage should outlive the cursor during its use.

functions.name: protocol::HttpChunkCursor::next
functions.description: Advances to the next chunk in the body, returning a pointer to the chunk data and its size. Returns true on success, false on end or failure.
requirements: chunk must be a non-null pointer to a const void* output location.
size must be a non-null pointer to a size_t output location.
The cursor must be initialized with a valid message and in a valid state.
The returned chunk pointer points into underlying storage; lifetime/ownership are unspecified and likely tied to the message.

functions.name: protocol::HttpChunkCursor::rewind
functions.description: Resets the chunk cursor to the beginning of the body, allowing iteration from the first chunk again.
requirements: The cursor must be initialized with a valid HttpMessage.
Any previously obtained chunk pointers may be invalidated by rewinding or subsequent operations.

functions.name: redis_parser_init
functions.description: Initializes a redis_parser_t instance to begin parsing Redis protocol replies. Call this before feeding any data to the parser.
requirements: parser must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory
Call this before any other redis_parser_* function on the same parser instance

functions.name: redis_parser_deinit
functions.description: Releases resources held by a redis_parser_t previously initialized with redis_parser_init. Intended to clean up any internal buffers/state after parsing is complete.
requirements: parser must be a valid, non-null pointer
parser should have been initialized with redis_parser_init before calling this function
Do not use the parser for further parsing after deinit unless re-initialized

functions.name: redis_parser_append_message
functions.description: Appends a chunk of bytes to the parser and advances parsing of Redis replies. The function processes data from buf according to the Redis protocol and updates the parser’s internal state and output reply accordingly. The size parameter is passed by pointer, typically to indicate the length of buf and/or to receive the number of bytes consumed.
requirements: buf must point to a readable memory buffer if *size > 0
size must be a valid, non-null pointer to the size (in bytes) of the input buffer
parser must be a valid, non-null pointer and should be initialized via redis_parser_init before calling
The memory at buf must remain valid for the duration of the call

functions.name: redis_reply_deinit
functions.description: Releases resources owned by a redis_reply_t (e.g., recursively freeing array elements or any owned buffers) that was produced or populated by the parser or helper functions.
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer
Only call on replies that were previously initialized/populated; after deinit the reply should not be used unless reinitialized

functions.name: redis_reply_set_array
functions.description: Configures a redis_reply_t as an array reply with the given element count, allocating/assigning its element vector accordingly.
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer
size specifies the number of array elements to hold; it should be the intended element count

functions.name: redis_reply_init
functions.description: Initializes a redis_reply_t to a NIL/empty state, clearing numeric value, lengths, and pointers. Useful before populating a reply manually.
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable memory

functions.name: redis_reply_set_string
functions.signature: static inline void redis_reply_set_string(const char *str, size_t len, redis_reply_t *reply);
functions.description: Marks the reply as a bulk string and assigns a pointer to an external string buffer and its length. No copy is performed.
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer
str must be a valid pointer to a buffer of at least len bytes and remain valid for as long as the reply is used
len must match the actual length of the string data

functions.name: redis_reply_set_integer
functions.signature: static inline void redis_reply_set_integer(long long intv, redis_reply_t *reply);
functions.description: Marks the reply as an integer and sets its numeric value.
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer

functions.name: redis_reply_set_null
functions.description: Marks the reply as NIL (null).
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer

functions.name: redis_reply_set_error
functions.signature: static inline void redis_reply_set_error(const char *err, size_t len, redis_reply_t *reply);
functions.description: Marks the reply as an error and assigns a pointer to an external error message buffer and its length. No copy is performed.
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer
err must be a valid pointer to a buffer of at least len bytes and remain valid for as long as the reply is used
len must match the actual length of the error string data

functions.name: redis_reply_set_status
functions.signature: static inline void redis_reply_set_status(const char *str, size_t len, redis_reply_t *reply);
functions.description: Marks the reply as a status string and assigns a pointer to an external status buffer and its length. No copy is performed.
requirements: reply must be a valid, non-null pointer
str must be a valid pointer to a buffer of at least len bytes and remain valid for as long as the reply is used
len must match the actual length of the status string data

functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a deep copy of another RedisValue, including contained string/array/integer content as applicable.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::RedisValue

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_nil
functions.description: Sets the value to nil (Redis NULL). Frees any previous content and changes the type to nil.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_int
functions.description: Sets the value to an integer with the given 64-bit value.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_string

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_string
functions.signature: void protocol::RedisValue::set_string(const char* str, size_t len)
functions.description: Sets the value to a bulk string from a character buffer and length.
requirements: str must point to a buffer of at least len bytes if len > 0.
If len is 0, str may be null or non-null; content becomes empty string (implementation details of null handling are not documented).

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_string
functions.description: Sets the value to a bulk string from a null-terminated C-string.
requirements: str must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_status
functions.description: Sets the value to a status string using an std::string (Redis simple string).

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_status
functions.signature: void protocol::RedisValue::set_status(const char* str, size_t len)
functions.description: Sets the value to a status (simple) string from a character buffer and length.
requirements: str must point to a buffer of at least len bytes if len > 0.
If len is 0, str may be null or non-null; resulting string is empty (exact null handling not documented).

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_status
functions.description: Sets the value to a status (simple) string from a null-terminated C-string.
requirements: str must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_error
functions.description: Sets the value to an error string using an std::string (Redis error reply).

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_error
functions.signature: void protocol::RedisValue::set_error(const char* str, size_t len)
functions.description: Sets the value to an error string from a character buffer and length.
requirements: str must point to a buffer of at least len bytes if len > 0.
If len is 0, str may be null or non-null; resulting string is empty (exact null handling not documented).

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_error
functions.description: Sets the value to an error string from a null-terminated C-string.
requirements: str must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set_array
functions.description: Sets the value type to an array and resizes it to new_size. Existing contents are replaced.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::set
functions.description: Populates this RedisValue from a C-style redis_reply_t (compatible with hiredis redisReply). Intended for interop with C parsers or libraries.
requirements: reply must point to a valid, fully-initialized redis_reply_t structure for the lifetime of this call.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::is_ok
functions.description: Returns true if the value is not an error type.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::is_error
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an error type.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::is_nil
functions.description: Returns true if the value is nil.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::is_int
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an integer.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::is_array
functions.description: Returns true if the value is an array.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::is_string
functions.description: Returns true if the value is a string or status (simple string). Errors are not considered by this predicate.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::get_type
functions.description: Returns the underlying type code (REDIS_REPLY_TYPE_*).

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::string_value
functions.description: Returns a copy of the contained string/status/error. If the type is not string/status/error, returns an empty string.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::string_view
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal std::string if the type is string/status/error; otherwise returns nullptr. No copy is made.
requirements: The returned pointer, if non-null, is only valid while this RedisValue remains alive and unchanged.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::int_value
functions.description: Returns the contained integer if the type is integer; otherwise returns 0.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::arr_size
functions.description: Returns the number of elements if the type is array; otherwise returns 0.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::arr_clear
functions.description: Clears all elements if the value is an array; otherwise does nothing.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::arr_resize
functions.description: Resizes the array to new_size if the value is an array; otherwise does nothing.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::arr_at
functions.description: Returns a reference to the element at index pos via std::vector::at(), which performs bounds checking and may throw on out-of-range.
requirements: pos must be less than arr_size(); otherwise std::out_of_range may be thrown.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::operator[]
functions.description: Returns a reference to the element at index pos via operator[] without bounds checking.
requirements: pos must be a valid index in the array; otherwise behavior is undefined.
The value must be of array type before indexing.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::transform
functions.description: Transforms this value into a C-style redis_reply_t structure. Useful for writing responses via C interop. Returns whether the transformation succeeded. Detailed semantics are not documented in this header.
requirements: reply must point to a valid, writable redis_reply_t structure.

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::clear
functions.description: Clears the value, equivalent to set_nil().

functions.name: protocol::RedisValue::debug_string
functions.description: Formats the value to a human-readable text representation for debugging. Exact format is not documented.

functions.name: protocol::RedisRequest::get_params

functions.name: protocol::RedisResponse::set_result

functions.name: protocol::RedisResponse::result_ptr
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the internal redis_reply_t result structure (same layout as hiredis redisReply). Not a copy; do not free this pointer.
requirements: The returned pointer must not be freed or reallocated by the caller.
The pointer remains valid only while the RedisResponse object and its internal parser state remain alive.

functions.name: mysql_stream_init
functions.description: Initializes a mysql_stream_t instance. Sets up internal bookkeeping for MySQL packet framing (header/payload tracking) and prepares the stream for subsequent operations (e.g., writing, sequence access). Exact fields initialized and whether the write callback is set are not shown in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: stream must be a non-null pointer to valid, writable mysql_stream_t storage.
Call this before any other operation that relies on initialized stream state (e.g., mysql_stream_write, mysql_stream_get_seq, mysql_stream_get_buf).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown from this header; treat a stream as not thread-safe unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: mysql_stream_write
functions.signature: static inline int mysql_stream_write(const void *buf, size_t *n, mysql_stream_t *stream);
functions.description: Delegates a write operation to the stream's underlying write callback (stream->write). The callback is responsible for consuming data from buf, updating *n to reflect processed bytes, and returning a status code. Specific semantics (blocking, partial writes, error codes) are not defined in this header and are unknown.
requirements: stream must be non-null and must have been initialized such that stream->write is a valid function pointer.

buf must be non-null and point to a readable memory region of at least *n bytes (the exact in/out convention for *n is not specified; commonly it is input size on entry and updated to bytes consumed on return).
n must be non-null and point to a writable size_t used by the callback to communicate the byte count.
The return value and error code conventions are callback-defined and not specified here; callers must handle nonzero/negative returns according to the implementation of stream->write.
This function is a thin inline wrapper; any threading or reentrancy guarantees are those of the underlying callback and are unknown here.

functions.name: mysql_stream_get_seq
functions.description: Returns the current MySQL packet sequence ID of the stream. The underlying field is an unsigned char; this function promotes it to int for return.
requirements: stream must be non-null and in a valid/initialized state.
Returned value is in the range [0, 255] due to the underlying unsigned char storage.

functions.name: mysql_stream_get_buf
functions.signature: static inline void mysql_stream_get_buf(const void **buf, size_t *length, mysql_stream_t *stream);
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the stream's internal buffer and its current length. The buffer is exposed as read-only via const void**; ownership remains with the stream. The lifetime/validity of the buffer relative to subsequent operations is not defined in this header and is unknown.
requirements: stream must be non-null and in a valid/initialized state.
buf must be non-null and will receive a pointer to the internal buffer; the caller must not free or write to this memory.
length must be non-null and will receive the size, in bytes, of the internal buffer content.
Validity of the returned pointer across subsequent calls (e.g., writes) is unspecified here; callers should not assume it remains stable unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: mysql_stream_deinit
functions.description: Deinitializes a mysql_stream_t by freeing its internal buffer (stream->buf). Does not null the pointer or reset other fields. After this call, the internal buffer must not be used.
requirements: stream must be non-null.
Call at most once per initialization; calling multiple times without reinitializing may lead to double free.
After deinit, any previously obtained buffer pointer from mysql_stream_get_buf becomes invalid and must not be used.
Do not access freed internal memory; reinitialize with mysql_stream_init before reuse.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::get_parser
functions.description: Returns the underlying MySQL protocol parser associated with this message. Useful for advanced users needing direct access to the low-level parser state.
requirements: May return nullptr if the parser has not been initialized; callers must check for null before use.
The returned pointer is owned by MySQLMessage; do not free it or store beyond the lifetime of the MySQLMessage instance.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::get_seqid
functions.description: Returns the current MySQL packet sequence id for this message. The sequence id is the 1-byte packet counter used by the MySQL protocol.
requirements: Meaningful only after the message has been initialized/parsed or set via set_seqid().
Result is in the range [0, 255] as the underlying storage is uint8_t.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::set_seqid
functions.description: Sets the MySQL packet sequence id for this message.
requirements: seqid must be in the range [0, 255] (value is stored in a uint8_t).
Should be called before encode() to affect outgoing packets.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::get_command
functions.description: Returns the MySQL command code associated with this message (e.g., COM_QUERY).
requirements: Valid only if a command has been set/parsed for this message; otherwise the value may be unspecified.
Command codes are 1-byte values in the range [0, 255].

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::append
functions.description: Appends raw bytes of a MySQL packet stream into the message for decoding/assembly. Commonly used by a transport to feed received data into the parser.
requirements: buf must be a valid pointer to at least *size bytes of readable memory.

size must be a valid, non-null pointer. The value it points to supplies the input byte count; the function may update it to reflect the number of bytes consumed or remaining (exact convention depends on implementation not shown here).
May be called multiple times as more data arrives; callers should preserve message state between calls.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::encode
functions.signature: virtual int protocol::MySQLMessage::encode(struct iovec vectors[], int max)
functions.description: Serializes the message into one or more iovec segments for transmission over a socket.
requirements: vectors must point to an array with capacity for at least max elements.
max must be positive if encoding is expected to produce output; zero or negative values are not useful.
The returned value is typically the number of iovecs filled; check the implementation/return contract when integrating (not shown here).
The MySQLMessage must be in a properly initialized state (e.g., command/query set for requests) before calling.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::decode_packet
functions.signature: virtual int protocol::MySQLMessage::decode_packet(const unsigned char *buf, size_t buflen)
functions.description: Base-class packet decoder hook. In MySQLMessage it is a stub that returns 1, with concrete decoding provided by derived classes (e.g., MySQLResponse).
requirements: buf may be ignored by this base implementation; derived implementations require buf to be non-null and buflen to match the packet length.
Normally not called directly by users; used internally by append()/parsing pipeline.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::set_command
functions.description: Sets the MySQL command code for this message. Despite being const-qualified, it updates internal command state (likely via mutable/indirect state).
requirements: cmd must be a valid MySQL command code in the range [0, 255].
Should be called before encode() to build a request with the desired command.

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::MySQLMessage
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes an empty MySQLMessage with internal parser/stream state ready to be used by append()/encode().
requirements: No special requirements for construction.
Before encoding a request, callers should set relevant fields (e.g., command, sequence id, query in a derived class).

functions.name: protocol::MySQLMessage::MySQLMessage

functions.name: protocol::MySQLUtil::escape_string
functions.description: Escapes special characters in a string for use in MySQL text contexts. Intended to transform raw input into a form safe for inclusion in SQL statements (e.g., string literals) by escaping characters MySQL treats specially. Typical usage: call before embedding user-provided text into SQL when manual string construction is unavoidable. Specific escape rules (which characters are escaped, encoding assumptions, and whether backslash or other modes are used) are not documented here and are unknown from this header; consult implementation or MySQL docs. Prefer parameterized queries when possible.
requirements: Input str must be a valid std::string; it may be empty.
No object state is required; method is static.
Behavior for encodings and which characters are escaped is unknown from this header.
Callers should not assume this provides full SQL injection protection; use parameterized queries where possible.
Function may allocate memory for the returned string; callers must handle potential allocation failures via exceptions in C++ (e.g., std::bad_alloc).

functions.description: Escapes a string for MySQL, additionally handling a specified quote character. Intended for preparing text to be embedded inside SQL literals delimited by a particular quote character (e.g., single or double quotes). Likely escapes occurrences of the provided quote in str and other MySQL-special characters. Whether the function also wraps the result in the quote character, and the exact set of escape rules, are not documented and are unknown from this header; consult implementation.
requirements: Input str must be a valid std::string; it may be empty.
quote should be the literal delimiter you intend to use in SQL (commonly '\'' or '"'); other values are permitted as char but resulting behavior is unspecified by this header.
No object state is required; method is static.
Whether the function surrounds the output with the quote character is unknown from this header; callers must not assume wrapping occurs.
Function may allocate memory for the returned string; callers must handle potential allocation failures via exceptions in C++ (e.g., std::bad_alloc).

functions.description: Decodes a MySQL length-encoded integer from the buffer range [*pos, end), storing the result in *res and advancing *pos past the encoded value. Intended to be bounds-safe (does not read beyond end). Return value semantics are not documented here.
requirements: res must be non-null.
pos must be non-null and *pos must be a valid pointer within the same buffer as end.
end must be non-null; *pos <= end on entry.
The buffer must contain a complete length-encoded integer at *pos; on insufficient data the function may fail and return a non-zero code (exact codes unknown).
Caller must check the return value and not use outputs on failure (exact conventions unknown).

functions.name: decode_string
functions.signature: int decode_string(const unsigned char **str, unsigned long long *len, const unsigned char **pos, const unsigned char *end)
functions.description: Decodes a MySQL length-encoded string from the buffer range [*pos, end). On success, sets *len to the decoded length, *str to point at the string payload within the buffer, and advances *pos past the payload. Return value semantics are not documented here.
requirements: str, len, and pos must be non-null; *str is set on success.
end must be non-null; *pos must be a valid pointer within the same buffer as end and satisfy *pos <= end on entry.
The buffer at *pos must contain a valid length-encoded integer followed by that many bytes of string data within end.
Caller must check the return value and only read *str/*len on success (exact codes unknown).
The returned *str points into the original buffer; the data is not null-terminated unless the encoded length includes a terminator.

functions.name: UpstreamManager::upstream_create_round_robin
functions.signature: static int UpstreamManager::upstream_create_round_robin(const std::string& name, bool try_another)
functions.description: Create an upstream group using round-robin selection. Call this once per upstream name to initialize the group before adding servers. If try_another is true, the manager will move to the next server when the initially chosen one is down; otherwise the request fails immediately.
requirements: name must identify a new or valid upstream namespace; creation fails with errno on error
Call this before adding servers to the upstream
try_another controls failover behavior when the first selected server is down: false = fail request; true = choose the next server

functions.name: UpstreamManager::upstream_create_consistent_hash
functions.signature: static int UpstreamManager::upstream_create_consistent_hash(const std::string& name, upstream_route_t consitent_hash)
functions.description: Create an upstream group using consistent-hash selection. The routing function determines the hash for a request and must return a non-negative value in the specified range. If the routing function is null, a default std::hash over the request URI is used.
requirements: name must identify the upstream to be created
consitent_hash may be nullptr; if nullptr, upstream uses std::hash with request URI
If provided, consitent_hash must return a value in [0, 2^31 - 1]
Create the upstream before adding servers to it

functions.name: UpstreamManager::upstream_create_weighted_random
functions.signature: static int UpstreamManager::upstream_create_weighted_random(const std::string& name, bool try_another)
functions.description: Create an upstream group using weighted-random selection. When try_another is true and the initially chosen server is down, the manager will choose among alive servers by weight; otherwise the request fails.
requirements: name must identify the upstream to be created
Call this before adding servers to the upstream
try_another=false: if the first chosen server is down, the request fails
try_another=true: if the first chosen server is down, choose from alive servers by weighted-random strategy

functions.name: UpstreamManager::upstream_create_manual
functions.signature: static int UpstreamManager::upstream_create_manual(const std::string& name, upstream_route_t select, bool try_another, upstream_route_t consitent_hash)
functions.description: Create an upstream group using manual selection. The select function determines the main server index. If try_another is true and the selected server is down, failover uses consistent hashing; if consitent_hash is null, a default std::hash over the request URI is used. If try_another is false, failure occurs immediately and the consistent-hash value is ignored.
requirements: name must identify the upstream to be created
select must not be nullptr
try_another=false: if first chosen server is down, request fails; consitent_hash is ignored
try_another=true: failover operates in consistent-hash mode; if consitent_hash==nullptr, std::hash over request URI is used
Create the upstream before adding servers to the upstream

functions.name: UpstreamManager::upstream_create_vnswrr
functions.description: Create an upstream group using VNSWRR (virtual node smooth weighted round-robin) selection. Use when smooth weighted RR behavior is desired.
requirements: name must identify the upstream to be created
Create the upstream before adding servers to the upstream

requirements: The upstream identified by name must already exist (created by one of the upstream_create_* functions)
address must be one of: ip, host, ip:port, host:port, or /unix-domain-socket string

address must be one of: ip, host, ip:port, host:port, or /unix-domain-socket string

functions.name: RouteManager::RouteTarget::init
functions.signature: int RouteManager::RouteTarget::init(const struct sockaddr *addr, socklen_t addrlen, SSL_CTX *ssl_ctx, int connect_timeout, int ssl_connect_timeout, int response_timeout, size_t max_connections)
functions.description: Initializes a RouteTarget (a CommSchedTarget) with the provided address, timeouts, max connection count, and optional SSL context. On success, it increments the SSL_CTX reference count when ssl_ctx is non-null. Intended to prepare a target for use by the communication scheduler.

Must be called before using the RouteTarget with the scheduler.

After deinit, the RouteTarget must not be used until re-initialized.

functions.description: Factory method that creates a new WFConnection for a given connected file descriptor. In this implementation, a fresh WFConnection is allocated and returned; the connect_fd is not used by the constructor here.

functions.description: Retrieves or creates routing/scheduling information for a target endpoint based on transport type, address info, endpoint parameters, and optional TLS context and hostname. On success, fills the provided RouteResult with a cookie and a request_object for use with the communication scheduler. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not documented).

functions.name: WFFuture<RES>::wait
functions.description: Blocks the calling thread until the associated asynchronous result is ready. Integrates with WFGlobal::sync_operation_begin/end while waiting when the result is not yet ready.
requirements: The underlying std::future<RES> must be valid before calling (i.e., valid() returns true).
May block the calling thread until the result becomes ready.
Safe to call multiple times; returns immediately if already ready.

functions.name: WFFuture<RES>::wait_for
functions.signature:
template<class REP, class PERIOD>
std::future_status WFFuture<RES>::wait_for(const std::chrono::duration<REP, PERIOD>& time_duration) const;
functions.description: Waits for the result for the specified duration and returns its readiness status. Uses WFGlobal::sync_operation_begin/end while waiting if not already ready.
requirements: The underlying std::future<RES> must be valid before calling.
Caller must provide a valid std::chrono::duration value.
May block the calling thread for up to the specified duration.
Returns std::future_status::ready if the result is already ready or becomes ready within the duration; otherwise returns timeout or deferred per std::future semantics.

functions.name: WFFuture<RES>::wait_until
functions.signature:
template<class CLOCK, class DURATION>
std::future_status WFFuture<RES>::wait_until(const std::chrono::time_point<CLOCK, DURATION>& timeout_time) const;
functions.description: Waits until the specified time point for the result and returns its readiness status. Uses WFGlobal::sync_operation_begin/end while waiting if not already ready.
requirements: The underlying std::future<RES> must be valid before calling.
Caller must provide a valid std::chrono::time_point.
May block the calling thread until the specified time point.
Returns std::future_status::ready if the result is already ready or becomes ready before the time point; otherwise returns timeout or deferred per std::future semantics.

functions.name: WFFuture<RES>::get
functions.description: Blocks until the result is ready (if needed) and then retrieves the result value from the associated std::future. Internally calls wait() first to integrate with WFGlobal before invoking std::future::get().
requirements: The underlying std::future<RES> must be valid before calling.
get() may be called at most once for a given future; subsequent calls will be invalid per std::future semantics.
May block the calling thread until the result becomes ready.
If the asynchronous operation stored an exception, that exception will be rethrown by get() per std::future semantics.

functions.name: WFFuture<RES>::valid
functions.description: Returns whether the underlying std::future currently refers to a shared state (i.e., whether it is valid).
requirements: None beyond having a WFFuture<RES> object; this is a non-blocking query.

functions.name: WFPromise<RES>::get_future
functions.description: Obtains a WFFuture<RES> connected to this promise, wrapping the underlying std::promise::get_future() result.
requirements: May be called at most once on a given WFPromise<RES>; multiple calls are invalid per std::promise semantics.
The promise must be valid (not moved-from).
The returned future will become ready when set_value() or set_exception() (not shown here) is called.

functions.name: WFPromise<RES>::set_value
functions.description: Fulfills the promise by setting the result value (copy) for the associated future, using the underlying std::promise::set_value().
requirements: May be called at most once for a given promise; calling again is invalid per std::promise semantics.
The promise must be valid (not moved-from) and must not already have a value or exception set.
The argument must be a value of type RES that is copyable into the promise.

functions.name: WFFuture<void>::get
functions.description: Blocks until the void result is ready (if needed) and then marks the future as retrieved, rethrowing any stored exception. Specialized for RES = void; internally calls wait() and then std::future<void>::get().
requirements: The underlying std::future<void> must be valid before calling.
get() may be called at most once for a given future; subsequent calls are invalid per std::future semantics.
May block the calling thread until the result becomes ready.
If the asynchronous operation stored an exception, that exception will be rethrown by get().

functions.name: WFPromise<void>::get_future
functions.description: Obtains a WFFuture<void> connected to this void promise, wrapping the underlying std::promise<void>::get_future().
requirements: May be called at most once on a given WFPromise<void>; multiple calls are invalid per std::promise semantics.
The promise must be valid (not moved-from).

functions.name: WFPromise<void>::set_value
functions.description: Fulfills the void promise by marking the result as ready for the associated future, using the underlying std::promise<void>::set_value().
requirements: May be called at most once for a given promise; calling again is invalid per std::promise semantics.
The promise must be valid (not moved-from) and must not already have a value or exception set.

functions.name: WFFacilities::usleep
functions.description: Sleeps the current thread for the specified number of microseconds. Synchronous/blocking variant of the timer utility.

Calling thread will block for approximately the specified duration.

functions.name: WFFacilities::async_usleep
functions.description: Schedules a non-blocking sleep for the specified number of microseconds and returns a future that becomes ready when the delay elapses.
requirements: Argument microseconds is an unsigned integer representing the delay in microseconds.
Caller should use/await the returned WFFuture<void> to detect completion.
Do not assume the future completes exactly at the requested time; completion timing may vary slightly.

static void WFFacilities::go(const std::string& queue_name, FUNC&& func, ARGS&&... args);

functions.name: WFFacilities::request
functions.signature:
template<class REQ, class RESP>

functions.description: Performs a synchronous network request using the specified transport type to the given URL with the provided request object. Returns a WFNetworkResult with the response object and task state/error information.
requirements: type selects the transport to use (exact enum values are library-defined/unknown).

retry_max is the maximum number of retries; non-negative expected by convention (exact semantics unknown).

functions.name: WFFacilities::async_request
functions.signature:
template<class REQ, class RESP>
static WFFuture<WFFacilities::WFNetworkResult<RESP>> WFFacilities::async_request(enum TransportType type, const std::string& url, REQ&& req, int retry_max);
functions.description: Initiates an asynchronous network request with the given transport, URL, and request object. Returns a future resolving to WFNetworkResult with the response and task state/error codes.
requirements: type selects the transport to use (exact enum values are library-defined/unknown).
url must be a properly formatted URL for the chosen transport (exact accepted formats are library-defined/unknown).
REQ must be a request type appropriate for the chosen transport and compatible with the framework (details unknown).
RESP must match the expected response type for the given transport/request (details unknown).
retry_max is the maximum number of retries; non-negative expected by convention (exact semantics unknown).
Caller should use/await the returned future and examine task_state and task_error to determine success/failure.

functions.name: WFFacilities::async_pread
functions.signature: static WFFuture<ssize_t> WFFacilities::async_pread(int fd, void *buf, size_t count, off_t offset);
functions.description: Asynchronously reads up to count bytes from the file associated with fd at the given offset into buf, without changing the file offset. Returns a future resolving to the read byte count or a negative error code per POSIX semantics.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor readable at the time of operation.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least count bytes that remains valid for the duration of the asynchronous read.
count specifies the maximum number of bytes to read.
offset specifies the file position to read from; must be a valid offset for the file (non-negative for regular files by POSIX convention).
Caller should await/use the returned WFFuture<ssize_t> and handle short reads and negative error returns in the result.

functions.name: WFFacilities::async_pwrite
functions.signature: static WFFuture<ssize_t> WFFacilities::async_pwrite(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count, off_t offset);
functions.description: Asynchronously writes up to count bytes from buf to the file associated with fd at the given offset, without changing the file offset. Returns a future resolving to the number of bytes written or a negative error code per POSIX semantics.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor writable at the time of operation.
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least count bytes that remains valid for the duration of the asynchronous write.
count specifies the maximum number of bytes to write.
offset specifies the file position to write to; must be a valid offset for the file (non-negative for regular files by POSIX convention).

functions.name: ParsedURI::ParsedURI
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes all URI component pointers to NULL and sets state to URI_STATE_INIT and error to 0. Use to create an empty, ready-to-parse URI object. Memory for components will be managed by the class RAII semantics.
requirements: No arguments required.
Constructed object must be destroyed exactly once to release any allocated component memory (handled by the destructor).
Do not manually free component pointers; they are owned by the ParsedURI instance.

functions.name: ParsedURI::ParsedURI
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a deep copy of another ParsedURI, duplicating all component strings and copying state/error. Useful for preserving a parsed URI snapshot.
requirements: The source uri must be a valid ParsedURI object.
Does a deep copy of component strings; caller must still not free component pointers on either instance.
Object must be destroyed exactly once to free its own copies of components.

functions.name: ParsedURI::ParsedURI
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership of component pointers and state from another ParsedURI, leaving the source in a valid but reset/unspecified state. Efficiently constructs from a temporary or movable URI.
requirements: The source uri must be an rvalue (temporary or explicitly std::move).
After move, use the source only for destruction or re-assignment; do not access its component pointers.

functions.name: ParsedURI::~ParsedURI
functions.description: Destructor. Frees any allocated component strings (scheme, userinfo, host, port, path, query, fragment). Called automatically on scope exit or delete. Leaves no allocated memory for components.
requirements: Do not use the ParsedURI instance after destruction.
Do not manually call the destructor; prefer automatic scope end or delete.
Component pointers must not be freed by the caller; they are freed here.

functions.name: ParsedURI::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces this instance’s contents with a deep copy of another ParsedURI, freeing any existing components first.
requirements: Safe for self-assignment (explicitly checked).
The source uri must be a valid ParsedURI object.
After assignment, previously held component memory in the destination is released; caller must not hold raw pointers into components across assignment.

functions.name: ParsedURI::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Frees current components and takes ownership of another ParsedURI’s component pointers and state, leaving the source in a valid but reset/unspecified state.
requirements: The source uri must be an rvalue (temporary or explicitly std::move).
Safe to assign over an existing ParsedURI; existing components are released first.
After move, use the source only for destruction or re-assignment; do not access its component pointers.
Do not keep raw pointers into the destination’s components across this operation; they may be invalidated.

functions.name: URIParser::parse
functions.signature: static int URIParser::parse(const char *str, ParsedURI& uri)
functions.description: Parses a URI from a null-terminated C string into the provided ParsedURI object. On success returns 0 and populates component fields; on failure returns -1 and sets state/error accordingly. Intended as the primary parsing API for C-string input.
requirements: str should be a valid, non-null, null-terminated C string representing a URI.
uri must be a valid ParsedURI reference; its fields may be modified and memory for components may be allocated.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure.
On failure, consult uri.state (e.g., URI_STATE_INVALID/URI_STATE_ERROR) and uri.error for details (exact error meanings are not documented here).
The function may allocate memory for component strings; do not free them manually—let uri’s destructor manage them.

functions.name: URIParser::parse
functions.signature: static int URIParser::parse(const std::string& str, ParsedURI& uri)
functions.description: Parses a URI from a std::string into the provided ParsedURI object by delegating to the const char* overload. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: str should contain a valid URI in std::string form.
uri must be a valid ParsedURI reference; its fields may be modified and memory for components may be allocated.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success, -1 indicates failure.
On failure, consult uri.state and uri.error for details (exact error meanings are not documented here).
Do not free component pointers manually; let uri’s destructor manage them.

functions.name: URIParser::split_query_strict
functions.description: Splits a query string into a multimap-like structure mapping keys to all of their values. Intended to preserve multiple values per key. Exact rules for decoding, handling of empty keys/values, and percent-encoding are not documented here and thus unknown.
requirements: query should be the URI query component (with or without a leading '?'; behavior regarding a leading '?' is not documented).
Input may be empty; the function will return an empty map in that case (inferred typical behavior).
No guarantees are documented about URL decoding or normalization; callers should not assume percent-decoding unless verified.

functions.name: URIParser::split_query
functions.description: Splits a query string into a map from key to a single value per key. Compared to split_query_strict, this collapses multiple values; whether it keeps the first or last occurrence is not documented and thus unknown.
requirements: query should be the URI query component (with or without a leading '?'; behavior regarding a leading '?' is not documented).
If duplicate keys appear, which value is retained is unspecified here; callers should not rely on a particular choice without checking the implementation.
No guarantees are documented about URL decoding or normalization; callers should not assume percent-decoding unless verified.

functions.name: URIParser::split_path
functions.description: Splits a path string into its segments, likely using '/' as the delimiter. Exact handling of leading/trailing slashes, empty segments, and percent-decoding is not documented and thus unknown.
requirements: path should be the URI path component (absolute or relative).
Behavior for consecutive or leading/trailing '/' resulting in empty segments is not documented; callers should not assume trimming or filtering unless verified.
No guarantees are documented about URL decoding; callers should not assume percent-decoding unless verified.

functions.name: WFConnection::get_context
functions.description: Returns the current user-defined context pointer associated with this WFConnection instance. Intended for retrieving an opaque pointer previously set via set_context() or test_set_context(). Useful for attaching application-specific state to a connection.
requirements: The returned pointer is opaque; its lifetime/validity is managed by the caller and/or a deleter previously installed.
May be called at any time on a valid WFConnection instance; thread-safety characteristics beyond the atomic storage of the pointer are not documented.

functions.name: WFConnection::set_context
functions.description: Sets the connection’s context pointer and a deleter functor to be invoked with that pointer when the WFConnection is destroyed. Use this to associate an owned resource with the connection and ensure it is cleaned up automatically at destruction.
requirements: Parameter context may be any pointer value, including null.
Parameter deleter must be callable as deleter(void*). It will be stored and, if set, called from WFConnection’s destructor with the then-current context pointer.
Caller must ensure the deleter is safe to invoke at destruction time (e.g., no double-free, handles null if context is null).
Subsequent calls overwrite the previously stored deleter and context.

functions.name: WFConnection::set_context
functions.description: Sets the connection’s context pointer without specifying a deleter. Use when the context is not owned by WFConnection or does not require automatic cleanup.
requirements: Parameter context may be any pointer value, including null.
No deleter is set/changed by this overload; previously set deleter remains unchanged.
Caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of the context pointer unless a deleter has been previously installed.

functions.name: WFConnection::test_set_context
functions.description: Atomically compares the current context pointer with test_context; if equal, replaces it with new_context and sets the deleter. Returns new_context on success, or test_context on failure. Use to perform a conditional context update with deleter installation.
requirements: Parameters test_context and new_context may be any pointer values, including null.
If the compare-and-exchange succeeds, the deleter is replaced with the provided deleter, which must be callable as deleter(void*), and may be invoked at destruction with the then-current context.
Return value is either new_context (success) or test_context (failure); caller should compare the return to determine outcome.
Atomic compare_exchange_strong uses default memory ordering for std::atomic (sequentially consistent). No further synchronization guarantees for the deleter are documented.

functions.name: WFConnection::test_set_context
functions.description: Atomically compares the current context pointer with test_context; if equal, replaces it with new_context. Returns new_context on success, or test_context on failure. Use for conditional context updates without changing the deleter.
requirements: Parameters test_context and new_context may be any pointer values, including null.
Return value is either new_context (success) or test_context (failure); caller should compare the return to determine outcome.
Only the context pointer is modified; any previously set deleter remains unchanged.
Atomic compare_exchange_strong uses default memory ordering for std::atomic (sequentially consistent).

functions.name: WFTaskFactory::release_guard

requirements: Per comment: release_guard must be called after and only after the task is finished, typically in its callback.

msg is an opaque pointer passed to the next waiter; caller manages lifetime.

functions.name: WFTaskFactory::release_guard_safe
functions.signature: static int WFTaskFactory::release_guard_safe(const std::string& resource_name, void *msg);

requirements: resource_name must match an existing guard.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_sort_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = sort_callback_t<T>>
static WFSortTask<T> *create_sort_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                       T *first, T *last,
                                       CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that sorts the range [first, last) of elements of type T using the default comparator, and invokes the provided callback when the task completes. Intended for asynchronous/offloaded execution on a named worker queue.
requirements: T* first and T* last must define a valid contiguous half-open range [first, last); last must be reachable from first (no overflow) and may be equal to first for an empty range.
The memory in [first, last) must be accessible and writable for the duration of the task.
queue_name must name a valid execution queue in the underlying workflow system (exact semantics unknown; inferred from naming).
CB must be callable as void(WFSortTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until invocation.
Elements of type T must be movable and comparable with operator< (default comparator).
This function is asynchronous; callers should use the callback to observe completion or results.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_psort_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = sort_callback_t<T>>
static WFSortTask<T> *create_psort_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                        T *first, T *last,
                                        CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that performs a parallel sort (implementation-specific) on the range [first, last) using the default comparator, then calls the callback. Useful for larger datasets.
requirements: T* first and T* last must form a valid contiguous range [first, last).
Range memory must be accessible and writable during the task.
queue_name must reference a valid worker queue (unknown specifics).
CB must be callable as void(WFSortTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until it is invoked.
T must be movable and comparable with operator<.
Parallel execution may reorder threads; ensure no concurrent writes to [first, last) by the caller while the task runs.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_merge_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = merge_callback_t<T>>
static WFMergeTask<T> *create_merge_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                         T *first1, T *last1,
                                         T *first2, T *last2,
                                         T *d_first,
                                         CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that merges two sorted ranges [first1, last1) and [first2, last2) into a destination range beginning at d_first using the default comparator, then calls the callback. The result range length equals (last1-first1) + (last2-first2).
requirements: first1/last1 and first2/last2 must each define valid contiguous ranges; memory must be readable for both ranges during the task.
Both input ranges must be sorted with respect to operator< (default comparator).
d_first must point to a contiguous output range large enough to hold (last1-first1) + (last2-first2) elements and be writable for the duration of the task.
The destination range must not overlap either input range (to avoid undefined behavior), unless implementation explicitly supports it (not stated; treat as non-overlapping).
queue_name must name a valid execution queue (unknown specifics).
CB must be callable as void(WFMergeTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until invocation.
T must be movable/assignable for output.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_shuffle_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = shuffle_callback_t<T>>
static WFShuffleTask<T> *create_shuffle_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                             T *first, T *last,
                                             CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that randomly shuffles elements in the range [first, last) using an implementation-defined RNG, then invokes the callback.
requirements: T* first and T* last must define a valid contiguous writable range [first, last).
queue_name must name a valid execution queue (unknown specifics).
CB must be callable as void(WFShuffleTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until invocation.
Caller must not modify [first, last) concurrently with the task.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_remove_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = remove_callback_t<T>>
static WFRemoveTask<T> *create_remove_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                           T *first, T *last,
                                           T value,
                                           CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that removes elements equal to value from the range [first, last) (remove/erase-style algorithm) and invokes the callback. The algorithm compacts remaining elements toward the front; the logical new end is communicated via the task's output.
requirements: T* first and T* last must define a valid contiguous writable range [first, last).
Equality comparison between T and value must be valid (operator==).
queue_name must name a valid execution queue (unknown specifics).
CB must be callable as void(WFRemoveTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until invocation.
Caller must handle the resulting logical end position from the task's output; this function does not deallocate or resize containers.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_unique_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = unique_callback_t<T>>
static WFUniqueTask<T> *create_unique_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                           T *first, T *last,
                                           CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that removes consecutive duplicate elements from [first, last) (unique-style algorithm), keeping the first occurrence of each run, then invokes the callback. The compacted range end is available via the task's output.
requirements: T* first and T* last must define a valid contiguous writable range [first, last).
Equality comparison on T (operator==) must be valid for detecting duplicates.
queue_name must name a valid execution queue (unknown specifics).
CB must be callable as void(WFUniqueTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until invocation.
Caller must not concurrently modify the range during task execution and should use the reported new end from the task output.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_reverse_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = reverse_callback_t<T>>
static WFReverseTask<T> *create_reverse_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                             T *first, T *last,
                                             CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that reverses the order of elements in the range [first, last) in place, then invokes the callback.
requirements: T* first and T* last must define a valid contiguous writable range [first, last).
queue_name must name a valid execution queue (unknown specifics).
CB must be callable as void(WFReverseTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until invocation.
Caller must not modify [first, last) concurrently while the task runs.

functions.name: WFAlgoTaskFactory::create_rotate_task
functions.signature:
template<typename T, class CB = rotate_callback_t<T>>
static WFRotateTask<T> *create_rotate_task(const std::string& queue_name,
                                           T *first, T *middle, T *last,
                                           CB callback);
functions.description: Creates a thread task that rotates the elements in the range [first, last) so that the element pointed to by middle becomes the first element (std::rotate semantics), then invokes the callback.
requirements: T* first, T* middle, and T* last must denote a valid contiguous range with first <= middle <= last.
The range [first, last) must be writable for the duration of the task.
queue_name must name a valid execution queue (unknown specifics).
CB must be callable as void(WFRotateTask<T>*), and callback must remain valid until invocation.
Caller must not modify the range concurrently while the task runs.

functions.name: Workflow::create_series_work
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new SeriesWork starting with the given first task and an optional completion callback. The series is created but not started; the caller should call SeriesWork::start() or manually dispatch the first task later.
requirements: first must be a valid SubTask pointer; behavior is undefined if null.
callback may be empty (nullptr-equivalent) and is optional.
Caller owns the returned SeriesWork and is responsible for eventually starting or dismissing it, or otherwise ensuring its lifetime is managed (e.g., via completing tasks).

functions.name: Workflow::start_series_work
functions.description: Creates a SeriesWork for the given first task and immediately dispatches the first task to start execution. The SeriesWork object is allocated internally and not returned.
requirements: first must be a valid SubTask pointer; it will be dispatched immediately.
callback may be empty (nullptr-equivalent).
The series is started exactly once by this call; do not manually dispatch the same task again.

functions.name: Workflow::create_parallel_work
functions.description: Allocates and returns an empty ParallelWork with an optional completion callback. Caller can add SeriesWork instances to it and then start it later.
requirements: callback may be empty (nullptr-equivalent).
Caller owns the returned ParallelWork and is responsible for adding series (via add_series) and starting or dismissing it.

functions.name: Workflow::start_parallel_work
functions.signature: void Workflow::start_parallel_work(SeriesWork *const all_series[], size_t n, parallel_callback_t callback)
functions.description: Creates a ParallelWork from the provided array of series and immediately starts it by wrapping it in a series and dispatching. The ParallelWork object is not returned.
requirements: all_series must point to an array of at least n valid SeriesWork* elements.
Each element in all_series[0..n-1] should be a non-null pointer to a SeriesWork.
callback may be empty (nullptr-equivalent).
This call starts the work immediately; do not start the same ParallelWork again.

functions.name: SeriesWork::start
functions.description: Starts execution of the series by dispatching its first task. Intended to be called on a standalone series (not embedded in a ParallelWork).
requirements: Must not be called if the series is inside a ParallelWork (asserts that in_parallel is null).
The series must have a valid first task; it will be dispatched immediately.
Call only once per created series to avoid multiple dispatches.

functions.name: SeriesWork::dismiss
functions.description: Cancels and destroys a created SeriesWork that has not been started, recursively dismissing contained tasks and sub-works. Intended to be called on the root series to abandon execution before starting.
requirements: Must not be called if the series is inside a ParallelWork (asserts that in_parallel is null).
Call dismiss() only when you do not plan to start the created series.
Because the operation is recursive, call only on the root series (do not call on sub-series).

functions.name: SeriesWork::push_back
functions.description: Appends a task to the end of the series’ task queue. Actual implementation is in the source; used to build the linear sequence of tasks.
requirements: task must be a valid SubTask pointer.
Only call before or between executions where modifying the series’ structure is supported; exact timing constraints are unknown from this header.

functions.name: SeriesWork::push_front
functions.description: Prepends a task to the beginning of the series’ task queue. Actual implementation is in the source.
requirements: task must be a valid SubTask pointer.
Only call before or between executions where modifying the series’ structure is supported; exact timing constraints are unknown from this header.

functions.name: SeriesWork::get_context
functions.description: Returns the opaque user-defined context pointer associated with this series.
requirements: No special requirements; returns the pointer previously set via set_context or null if never set.

functions.name: SeriesWork::set_context
functions.description: Associates an opaque user-defined context pointer with this series for later retrieval.
requirements: context may be null; ownership and lifetime of the pointed-to object are managed by the caller.

functions.name: SeriesWork::cancel
functions.description: Marks the series as canceled. Typically called within a task’s callback belonging to the series. Subsequent tasks in the series will be destroyed immediately (including nested ParallelWork) without invoking their callbacks, but the series' own callback will still be called.
requirements: Should be called on a running series, typically from within a task callback. Exact timing is not enforced by the code here.
After cancellation, do not rely on callbacks of remaining tasks being invoked.

functions.name: SeriesWork::is_canceled
functions.description: Returns whether the series has been marked canceled.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SeriesWork::is_finished
functions.description: Returns whether the series has reached the time of its callback (i.e., finished). Mainly useful for subclasses.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SeriesWork::set_callback
functions.description: Sets or replaces the completion callback to be invoked when the series finishes (even if canceled).
requirements: callback may be empty (nullptr-equivalent).
If called after work started, ensure thread-safety/execution ordering as appropriate; exact guarantees are not specified here.

functions.name: SeriesWork::get_specific
functions.description: Retrieves a series-specific value by key. Default implementation returns null. Intended for subclass-specific data retrieval.
requirements: key must be a valid C string pointer; interpretation is subclass-defined.
Behavior is subclass-specific; default implementation always returns null.

functions.name: SeriesWork::pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the next SubTask from the series’ internal queue. Intended for task implementations only.
requirements: Intended to be called only by task implementations; external callers should not use this.
Only valid when the series maintains an internal queue; calling on an empty queue may return null depending on implementation (not specified here).

functions.name: SeriesWork::get_last_task
functions.description: Returns the task currently recorded as the last task of the series.
requirements: None; may return null if no last task is set.

functions.name: SeriesWork::set_last_task
functions.description: Sets the last task pointer for the series and assigns the series pointer into the task. Used when explicitly specifying the terminal task of the series.
requirements: last must be a valid SubTask pointer; it will have set_pointer(this) invoked on it.
Should be called before starting the series.

functions.name: SeriesWork::unset_last_task
functions.description: Clears the recorded last task pointer of the series.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SeriesWork::get_in_parallel
functions.description: Returns the ParallelTask that this series is currently part of, or null if it is not part of a parallel work.
requirements: None; callers can use a null return to detect standalone series.

functions.name: series_of
functions.description: Returns the SeriesWork that the given task belongs to by reading the task’s associated pointer.
requirements: task must be a valid SubTask pointer that has been associated with a SeriesWork via set_pointer; otherwise the result is invalid.

functions.name: operator*
functions.description: Convenience operator that dereferences a SubTask to its owning SeriesWork reference, equivalent to *series_of(&task).
requirements: task must belong to a SeriesWork and have its pointer set; otherwise results in undefined behavior.

functions.name: operator<<
functions.description: Convenience operator to append a task to a series, equivalent to series.push_back(task). Returns the series to allow chaining.
requirements: task must be a valid SubTask pointer.
Safe usage timing for modifying the series depends on implementation; not specified here.

functions.name: ParallelWork::start
functions.description: Starts execution of the parallel work by starting an internal series that wraps it. Intended to be called on a standalone ParallelWork (not already part of a SeriesWork).
requirements: Must not be already attached to a SeriesWork (asserts that series_of(this) is null).
Starts immediately; do not start the same instance more than once.

functions.name: ParallelWork::dismiss
functions.description: Destroys the ParallelWork without starting it. Intended for standalone instances not attached to a SeriesWork.
requirements: Must not be already attached to a SeriesWork (asserts that series_of(this) is null).
Only call when you do not intend to start this ParallelWork.

functions.name: ParallelWork::add_series
functions.description: Adds a SeriesWork to this ParallelWork for concurrent execution. Implementation is in the source file.
requirements: series must be a valid SeriesWork pointer.
The series should not be null and should be suitable for inclusion; exact lifecycle/ownership rules are not specified here.
Call before starting the ParallelWork.

functions.name: ParallelWork::get_context
functions.description: Returns the opaque user-defined context pointer associated with this parallel work.
requirements: No special requirements; returns the pointer previously set via set_context or null if never set.

functions.name: ParallelWork::operator[]

functions.name: ParallelWork::size

functions.name: ParallelWork::end

functions.name: ParallelWork::set_callback

functions.name: operator>

functions.description: Series composition: append a ParallelWork y to the end of SeriesWork x. Equivalent to x.push_back(&y). Enables chaining with further > operations.

Returned reference aliases x and remains valid as long as x is valid.

functions.name: operator*

functions.description: Parallel composition: add SeriesWork y as a branch to existing ParallelWork x. Equivalent to x.add_series(&y). Enables chaining with further * operations.
