y must be a valid, live SeriesWork reference.
Returned reference aliases x and remains valid as long as x is valid.

functions.name: WFResourcePool::get
functions.description: Asynchronously acquire a resource from the pool and deliver it to the caller via resbuf. The returned WFConditional can be used to wait until a resource is available and the acquisition completes. When the condition is satisfied, *resbuf is expected to point to the acquired resource. Exact wakeup semantics and threading behavior are not documented here and remain unknown.
requirements: task must be a valid (non-null) SubTask pointer associated with the workflow runtime (inferred from type usage).
resbuf must be non-null and point to writable storage for a void* where the acquired resource will be stored.
The caller should not free or otherwise destroy the resource; it must later be returned via WFResourcePool::post (inferred from pool semantics).
Behavior when the pool is exhausted or when task is cancelled is unknown; callers should be prepared for framework-defined behavior.

functions.name: WFResourcePool::post
functions.description: Return (release) a previously acquired resource back to the pool so that it can be reused by other tasks. Typical usage is to call post once the caller is finished with the resource obtained via get.
requirements: res should be a resource that originated from this WFResourcePool instance (inferred from resource-pool semantics).
Do not post the same resource more than once without a matching get (to avoid pool corruption; inferred).
Do not post null unless the pool is documented to accept null resources; acceptance of null is unknown.

functions.name: WFResourcePool::Data::pop
functions.description: Obtain a resource from the underlying pool by delegating to WFResourcePool::pop(). Intended for internal use by the pool’s data/queue handling. Returns a pointer to the next available resource. Thread-safety and blocking semantics are not documented here.
requirements: this->pool must be non-null and point to a valid WFResourcePool instance (explicit from implementation calling this->pool->pop()).
The returned resource must later be returned via Data::push or the corresponding pool mechanism (inferred).

functions.name: WFResourcePool::Data::push
functions.description: Return a resource to the underlying pool by delegating to WFResourcePool::push(res). Intended for internal use by the pool’s data/queue handling.
requirements: this->pool must be non-null and point to a valid WFResourcePool instance (explicit from implementation calling this->pool->push(res)).
res should be a resource previously obtained from the same pool (inferred).

functions.name: WFResourcePool::WFResourcePool
functions.description: Construct a resource pool initialized with an array of n resource pointers. The pool will manage these resources and hand them out to callers of get, expecting them to be returned via post.
requirements: res must point to a contiguous array of at least n pointers (explicit from signature and typical usage).
n specifies the number of resources; behavior for n == 0 is unknown.

Ownership and lifetime of the resource pointers themselves are managed by the caller or the pool depending on design; only the array storage for pointers is freed by the pool’s destructor as shown (the pool deletes only its internal res array, not the resources).

functions.name: WFResourcePool::~WFResourcePool
functions.description: Destroy the resource pool and release internal storage for the resource pointer array. The destructor deletes the internal data.res array but does not delete the resources the pointers may reference.
requirements: All resources should have been returned to the pool before destruction to avoid leaks or dangling ownership (inferred).
Do not use the pool or any WFConditional returned from it after destruction.

functions.name: WFMessageQueue::get
functions.description: Asynchronously (or conditionally) receive a message from the queue, integrating with a workflow SubTask. On completion, writes the received message pointer to *msgbuf and returns a WFConditional that can be used to wait for or chain the operation. Implementation is not present in this header; exact scheduling, blocking, and wake semantics are unknown.
requirements: msgbuf must be a non-null pointer to storage for a void* to receive the message pointer.
The SubTask* must be a valid pointer compatible with the workflow framework (exact lifetime and threading semantics are unknown).
Ownership/lifetime of the message pointer is not managed by the queue; producers/consumers must manage the pointed-to object's lifetime.

functions.name: WFMessageQueue::post
functions.description: Posts/enqueues a message pointer to the queue, potentially waking any waiters created via get. The queue stores the raw pointer and later returns it to a consumer; it does not copy or manage the pointed-to data.
requirements: msg is stored as a raw pointer without copying; the queue does not take ownership of the pointed-to data.
The pointed-to object must remain valid until it is retrieved by a consumer; producers/consumers must define and enforce ownership/lifetime.
Null pointers as messages are not documented; whether NULL is a valid message value is unknown.

functions.name: WFMessageQueue::Data::pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the next message from the underlying WFMessageQueue by delegating to queue->pop(). This simply returns the stored pointer; no memory management is performed on the pointed-to object.
requirements: Must only be called when the underlying queue contains at least one message; otherwise, queue->pop() will dereference an empty list and result in undefined behavior.
In concurrent contexts, callers must ensure external synchronization (e.g., lock data.mutex) around pop to prevent races; this method itself does not lock.
The returned value is the enqueued pointer; ownership/lifetime of the pointed-to object is managed by caller-side protocol.

functions.name: WFMessageQueue::Data::push
functions.description: Enqueues a message pointer into the underlying WFMessageQueue by delegating to queue->push(msg). The queue stores the pointer as-is without copying or taking ownership.
requirements: In concurrent contexts, callers must ensure external synchronization (e.g., lock data.mutex) around push to prevent races; this method itself does not lock.
msg is stored as a raw pointer; the queue does not manage the pointed-to object's lifetime.

functions.name: WFMessageQueue::WFMessageQueue
functions.description: Constructor that initializes the internal message and wait lists and sets the Data.back-pointer (data.queue) to this. Prepares the queue for use.
requirements: Must be called before any other member functions are used on the instance.
No messages are pre-allocated; users must post messages before attempting to pop/get.

functions.name: WFMessageQueue::~WFMessageQueue
functions.description: Virtual destructor that performs no cleanup of enqueued message pointers or external resources. Provided for safe polymorphic deletion.
requirements: Ensure no other threads are accessing the queue at destruction time to avoid races or use-after-free.
Any messages still enqueued at destruction are not freed; callers must ensure appropriate cleanup of pointed-to objects before destroying the queue.

functions.name: WFResolverTask::WFResolverTask
functions.signature: WFResolverTask::WFResolverTask(const struct WFNSParams *ns_params, unsigned int dns_ttl_default, unsigned int dns_ttl_min, const struct EndpointParams *ep_params, router_callback_t&& cb)
functions.description: Constructs a resolver task that performs DNS/name resolution using the provided name-service and endpoint parameters. The task uses the supplied default and minimum DNS TTL values to guide caching behavior and stores copies of ns_params and ep_params. If ns_params->fixed_conn is true, the task forces ep_params_.max_connections to 1. Usage: create this task with valid pointers to WFNSParams and EndpointParams and a completion callback; schedule the task within the framework to resolve a host/port determined later by dispatch(). Other operational details are internal to the workflow framework and not exposed here.
requirements: ns_params must be a non-null pointer to a fully initialized WFNSParams; it is dereferenced during construction.
ep_params must be a non-null pointer to a fully initialized EndpointParams; it is dereferenced during construction.
cb must be a valid router_callback_t callable; it will be moved into the base WFRouterTask.
dns_ttl_default and dns_ttl_min are unsigned integers; no explicit range constraints are documented.
If ns_params->fixed_conn is true, max_connections will be forced to 1 in the stored EndpointParams copy.

functions.name: WFResolverTask::WFResolverTask
functions.description: Constructs a resolver task using only name-service parameters and a completion callback. Endpoint parameters are left at their default-initialized state, except that if ns_params->fixed_conn is true, the task forces ep_params_.max_connections to 1. Usage: create this task when endpoint tuning is not provided and schedule within the framework; resolution specifics are handled internally during dispatch().
requirements: ns_params must be a non-null pointer to a fully initialized WFNSParams; it is dereferenced during construction.
cb must be a valid router_callback_t callable; it will be moved into the base WFRouterTask.
If ns_params->fixed_conn is true, max_connections will be forced to 1 in the task’s internal EndpointParams.

functions.name: UPSManualPolicy::first_strategy
functions.description: Manually selects an endpoint for the given URI using the primary route function provided at construction. Returns the chosen EndpointAddress pointer or nullptr on failure (exact conditions unknown).
requirements: uri must be a valid ParsedURI.
tracing may be null if tracing is optional; exact usage is unspecified.
Caller must handle a possible null return pointer, indicating selection failure.

functions.name: UPSManualPolicy::another_strategy
functions.description: Attempts an alternate manual selection strategy for the given URI using the secondary route function provided at construction. Returns an EndpointAddress pointer or nullptr on failure (exact conditions unknown).
requirements: Typically used when try_another was set true at construction; behavior otherwise is unspecified.
uri must be a valid ParsedURI.
tracing may be null if optional; exact usage is unspecified.
Caller must handle a possible null return pointer.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate interesting, valid filesystem paths that the fuzzer will use to create/open files.
# Goals:
# - Prefer relative paths pointing into an existing writable temp directory.
# - Include a variety of components: simple names, nested dirs, dot/hidden names, spaces, unicode, long names.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes.
# - Avoid characters that are invalid on common platforms (e.g., NUL, path separators inside a component list handled by joining).
# - Do not perform any I/O; we only return a byte string path.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "数据", "テスト", "тест", "prøve", "δοκιμή", "اختبار", "परीक्षण", "테스트",
    "文件", "файл", "dossier", "árvíztűrő", "mañana", "café"
]

SPECIAL_NAMES = [
    "tmp", "data", "input", "seed", "file", "buf", "out", "in",
    ".hidden", "..dot..", "space name", "tabs\tname", "dash-name", "under_score"
]

EXTS = ["", ".bin", ".dat", ".txt", ".log"]

# Common base directories that typically exist; use relative paths by default for portability.
BASES = [
    ".",  # current dir
    "./.",  # normalize
    "./tmp",
    "./work",
    "./out",
]


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    # Mix safe ascii and occasional unicode fragments
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.20:
        frag = rng.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS)
        tail_len = rng.randint(0, 6)
        tail = "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(tail_len))
        return frag + tail
    elif choice < 0.45:
        return rng.choice(SPECIAL_NAMES)
    else:
        n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
        s = "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n)).strip()
        if not s:
            s = "x"
        return s


def _rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(EXTS)


def _rand_components(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # 1 to 4 components after base
    depth = 1 + rng.randint(0, 3)
    comps = []
    for i in range(depth):
        name = _rand_name(rng)
        # Occasionally use very long name within safe limits
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            name = name + (rng.choice(["_", "-"]) * rng.randint(10, 40))
        # Append extension on last component sometimes
        if i == depth - 1 and rng.random() < 0.8:
            name = name + _rand_ext(rng)
        comps.append(name)
    return comps


def _maybe_nested_base(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(BASES)
    # Occasionally produce a nested base like ./tmp/subdir
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        sub = _rand_name(rng)
        base = os.path.join(base, sub)
    return base


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide between relative and absolute; prefer relative for portability
    absolute = rng.random() < 0.15

    if absolute:
        # Choose a likely existing absolute base, but keep it generic and Unix-like.
        # Consumers often rewrite/redirect, so path existence is not required.
        base_candidates = ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/dev/shm", "/"]
        base = rng.choice(base_candidates)
    else:
        base = _maybe_nested_base(rng)

    comps = _rand_components(rng)

    # Join safely; os.path.join handles separators for the running platform.
    path = os.path.join(base, *comps)

    # Trim to max length 4096 bytes
    encoded = path.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(encoded) > 4096:
        # Keep the end (filename) more intact by trimming from the left if needed
        encoded = encoded[-4096:]
        # Avoid starting mid-multibyte; re-decode safely
        path = encoded.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        encoded = path.encode("utf-8")

    return encoded

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: HTTP method token
# - Uppercase letters A-Z and hyphen '-'
# - Typical lengths 3-10, but fuzzers cap at 15/16
# - Examples: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS, HEAD, CONNECT, TRACE
# The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times expecting method-like tokens.

COMMON_METHODS = [
    b"GET", b"POST", b"PUT", b"DELETE", b"PATCH", b"OPTIONS",
    b"HEAD", b"CONNECT", b"TRACE", b"PROPFIND", b"MKCOL",
    b"COPY", b"MOVE", b"LOCK", b"UNLOCK", b"SEARCH",
]

EXOTIC_METHODS = [
    b"REPORT", b"CHECKOUT", b"MERGE", b"SUBSCRIBE", b"UNSUBSCRIBE",
    b"NOTIFY", b"PURGE", b"LINK", b"UNLINK", b"M-SEARCH",
    b"PRI", b"DESCRIBE", b"ANNOUNCE", b"SETUP", b"PLAY", b"PAUSE",
]

ALPHABET = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ-"

def rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 15) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(n))

def weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[bytes], weights: List[int]) -> bytes:
    total = sum(weights)
    x = rng.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if x < acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus = []
    # Prioritize common real methods
    corpus.extend(COMMON_METHODS)
    # Include some exotic/extension methods
    corpus.extend(EXOTIC_METHODS[:rng.randint(3, len(EXOTIC_METHODS))])
    # Include hyphenated tokens to hit '-' handling
    corpus.extend([b"M-SEARCH", b"CUSTOM-METHOD", b"X-FOO", b"X-BATCH-UPDATE"])  # within 15-16 chars
    # Random tokens of varying lengths including boundary sizes
    for L in [1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 10, 15, 16]:
        # Ensure at least one valid min (>=1) though fuzzer trims; we keep >=1
        L = max(1, min(16, L))
        tok = bytes(rng.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(L))
        # Ensure starts with letter to be more likely valid
        if tok and tok[0] == ord('-'):
            tok = bytes([rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ")]) + tok[1:]
        corpus.append(tok)
    # A few fully random tokens
    for _ in range(8):
        corpus.append(rand_token(rng))
    # Ensure presence of canonical short ones
    corpus.extend([b"GET", b"POST"])  # duplicates okay
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for m in corpus:
        if m not in seen:
            seen.add(m)
            uniq.append(m)
    return uniq

def package_strings(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Simple newline-delimited package; FUZZ_PARAM_STR in harness treats the
    # provided buffer generically as a byte source. Newlines are safe
    # delimiters for extracting multiple strings.
    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    chunks = []
    size = 0
    for s in strings:
        # Constrain to at most 16 bytes as stubs cap at 15/16
        s = s[:16]
        line = s + b"\n"
        if size + len(line) > 4096:
            break
        chunks.append(line)
        size += len(line)
    return b"".join(chunks)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = build_corpus(rng)
    # Randomize ordering slightly to provide variability per seed
    rng.shuffle(corpus)
    # Bias to place a few very common ones early to satisfy immediate calls
    head_candidates = [b"GET", b"POST", b"PUT", b"DELETE", b"HEAD"]
    # Make sure these are at the front (if present)
    prioritized = [m for m in head_candidates if m in corpus]
    rest = [m for m in corpus if m not in prioritized]
    rng.shuffle(rest)
    ordered = prioritized + rest
    return package_strings(ordered)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: HTTP reason phrase
# Fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR to set reason phrases.
# Requirements inferred from stubs and APIs:
# - Parser must be in response mode; phrases should be short (<=64) and printable (no < 0x20).
# - Empty strings are replaced by defaults in stubs, but we still generate meaningful ones.
# - Interesting values include: common phrases, unusual but valid tokens, varying lengths,
#   mixed case, punctuation, UTF-8, boundary lengths (1, 2, 63, 64), and with multiple words.
# - We return a bytes buffer that the harness will slice for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build multiple reason phrases separated by newlines (or NULs) so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can
#   read segments; many fuzz frameworks read sequential strings from the provided buffer.
# - Ensure each phrase is <= 64 bytes and contains only >= 0x20 characters (spaces allowed).
# - Include a mix: RFC classics, edge-length phrases, tokens with symbols, and some
#   randomized phrases using safe characters.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -._()/+:;'?,!@#$%^&*={}[]|~`"

COMMON_PHRASES = [
    "OK",
    "Not Found",
    "Created",
    "Accepted",
    "No Content",
    "Partial Content",
    "Moved Permanently",
    "Found",
    "See Other",
    "Temporary Redirect",
    "Permanent Redirect",
    "Bad Request",
    "Unauthorized",
    "Forbidden",
    "Internal Server Error",
    "Not Implemented",
    "Bad Gateway",
    "Service Unavailable",
    "Gateway Timeout",
    "HTTP Version Not Supported",
    "Switching Protocols",
    "Processing",
    "Too Many Requests",
    "Unavailable For Legal Reasons",
    "I'm a teapot",
]

SYMBOLIC_VARIANTS = [
    "All Good ✔",
    "Done ✅",
    "Teapot ☕",
    "Hmm… Maybe",
    "Upgraded/TLS",
    "Proxy Auth Required",
    "Range Not Satisfiable",
    "Unsupported Media Type",
    "Precondition Failed",
    "Expectation Failed",
]

# Sanitize to printable ASCII or leave basic UTF-8 symbols where safe.
# Since the stub replaces control chars with spaces, we avoid <0x20 entirely.

def _rand_phrase(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(L))
    # Ensure no leading/trailing spaces-only; collapse multiple spaces somewhat
    s = s.strip()
    if not s:
        s = "OK"
    return s[:64]


def _pad_to_boundary(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Create a phrase exactly target_len (<=64)
    base = _rand_phrase(rng, max(1, target_len // 2), target_len)
    if len(base) > target_len:
        base = base[:target_len]
    elif len(base) < target_len:
        base += ' ' * (target_len - len(base))
    return base[:64]


def _unique_keep(seq: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in seq:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    phrases: List[str] = []

    # 1) Include a shuffled subset of common phrases
    common = COMMON_PHRASES.copy()
    rng.shuffle(common)
    phrases.extend(common[:rng.randint(6, min(12, len(common)))])

    # 2) Include some symbolic/unicode-like variants but ensure length <= 64
    sym = SYMBOLIC_VARIANTS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(sym)
    phrases.extend(sym[:rng.randint(3, min(6, len(sym)))])

    # 3) Boundary lengths (1, 2, 63, 64)
    phrases.append(_pad_to_boundary(rng, 1))
    phrases.append(_pad_to_boundary(rng, 2))
    phrases.append(_pad_to_boundary(rng, 63))
    phrases.append(_pad_to_boundary(rng, 64))

    # 4) Random multi-word phrases
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 10)):
        words = rng.randint(2, 5)
        parts = [_rand_phrase(rng, 2, rng.randint(4, 12)) for _ in range(words)]
        s = ' '.join(p.strip() for p in parts if p)
        if not s:
            s = 'OK'
        phrases.append(s[:64])

    # 5) Case variants of a random base
    base = _rand_phrase(rng, 3, 12)
    phrases.extend([
        base.lower()[:64],
        base.upper()[:64],
        base.title()[:64],
        (base + "!!!")[:64],
    ])

    # 6) Phrases with punctuation mixes
    puncts = [":)", ":(", ";)", "#1", "v2.0", "alpha-beta", "retry?", "ok/ok", "{done}"]
    rng.shuffle(puncts)
    for p in puncts[:rng.randint(4, 7)]:
        s = (base + ' ' + p)[:64]
        phrases.append(s)

    # 7) Ensure at least one classic fallback and one long descriptive phrase
    phrases.append("OK")
    phrases.append("Operation Completed Successfully")

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    phrases = _unique_keep(phrases)

    # Ensure all are printable and <=64
    cleaned: List[str] = []
    for ph in phrases:
        # Remove control characters just in case
        ph2 = ''.join(ch if ord(ch) >= 0x20 else ' ' for ch in ph)
        ph2 = ph2.strip()
        if not ph2:
            ph2 = 'OK'
        cleaned.append(ph2[:64])

    # Join using NUL separators plus newline terminators to help various consumers
    # Limit total size to 4096 bytes
    out_bytes = bytearray()
    sep = b"\0\n"
    for s in cleaned:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > 64:
            b = b[:64]
        # each entry: b + sep
        if len(out_bytes) + len(b) + len(sep) > 4096:
            break
        out_bytes += b + sep

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not out_bytes:
        out_bytes = bytearray(b"OK\0\n")

    return bytes(out_bytes)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: HTTP header name (token per RFC7230): 1+ of tchar: ALPHA / DIGIT / '-'
# Fuzzer stubs also accept arbitrary names but sanitize to letters and '-'.
# We'll generate interesting, valid header names of varying patterns/sizes to
# exercise add/set/find and header-map behaviors.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

TOKEN_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '-'  # valid token set

# Some well-known header names to trigger special code paths (e.g., Connection, Content-Length)
KNOWN_HEADERS = [
    "Content-Length", "Content-Type", "Connection", "Host", "User-Agent",
    "Accept", "Accept-Encoding", "Transfer-Encoding", "Cookie", "Set-Cookie",
    "Cache-Control", "Pragma", "Upgrade", "Authorization", "Range",
    "If-Modified-Since", "ETag", "X-Fuzz", "Foo", "Bar"
]

# Value strings used alongside names in some stubs
COMMON_VALUES = [
    "keep-alive", "close", "gzip, deflate, br", "chunked", "no-cache",
    "max-age=0", "bytes=0-99", "text/plain", "application/json", "v"
]

def rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(TOKEN_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def interesting_header_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names: List[str] = []
    # Include some known headers
    names.extend(rng.sample(KNOWN_HEADERS, k=min(5, len(KNOWN_HEADERS))))
    # Edge lengths
    names.append(rand_token(rng, 1, 1))           # length 1
    names.append(rand_token(rng, 2, 2))           # length 2
    names.append(rand_token(rng, 62, 63))         # near fuzzer cap (<=63)
    # Patterns: repeated hyphens and mixed case
    base = rand_token(rng, 4, 8)
    names.append(base.lower())
    names.append(base.upper())
    names.append('-'.join([rand_token(rng, 3, 6) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))]))
    # A couple randoms
    for _ in range(6):
        names.append(rand_token(rng, 3, 16))
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for n in names:
        if n not in seen:
            seen.add(n)
            out.append(n)
    return out

def build_kv_blob(rng: random.Random, names: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # The fuzz harness calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times across stubs.
    # We'll provide a single buffer containing multiple NUL-terminated strings
    # so successive extractions get deterministic pieces. Include interleaved
    # names and values, plus extra targets like "Foo"/"Bar" for cursor tests.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Seed with some specific names to ensure presence
    seed_names = ["Foo", "Bar", "X-Fuzz", "Connection", "Content-Length"]
    for n in seed_names:
        parts.append(n.encode('ascii') + b"\x00")
    # Add the provided names
    for n in names:
        # Ensure only token chars (already enforced) and cap length <= 63
        s = n[:63]
        parts.append(s.encode('ascii') + b"\x00")
        # For each name, add a plausible value next
        val = rng.choice(COMMON_VALUES)
        parts.append(val.encode('ascii') + b"\x00")
    # Add some extra small/random values
    for _ in range(10):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(rand_token(rng, 1, 8).encode('ascii') + b"\x00")
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(COMMON_VALUES).encode('ascii') + b"\x00")
    blob = b''.join(parts)
    return blob[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    names = interesting_header_names(rng)
    blob = build_kv_blob(rng, names)
    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: HTTP header value (field-value). Should be visible text excluding CRLF.
# This generator produces a single bytes buffer that can be split/consumed by fuzzer stubs
# via FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls to supply reasonable HTTP header names/values and related strings.

VISIBLE_CHARS = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
)
# Exclude CR and LF explicitly
VISIBLE_CHARS = VISIBLE_CHARS.replace("\n", "").replace("\r", "")

# Some interesting but valid header values exercising different code paths
BASE_VALUES = [
    "keep-alive",
    "close",
    "gzip, deflate, br",
    "no-cache",
    "max-age=0",
    "text/html; charset=UTF-8",
    "application/json",
    "attachment; filename=example.txt",
    "bytes=0-",
    "chunked",
    "Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz",
    "Bearer abcdef0123456789",
    "W/\"etag-123\"",
    "*/*",
    "en-US,en;q=0.9",
    "Mon, 01 Jan 2024 00:00:00 GMT",
]

# Some header names that are valid tokens (only visible to seed some stubs that accidentally use value for name)
TOKEN_NAMES = [
    "Content-Type",
    "Content-Length",
    "Connection",
    "Transfer-Encoding",
    "Accept",
    "Accept-Encoding",
    "User-Agent",
    "Host",
    "X-Fuzz",
    "X-Test",
]


def _rand_visible(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(VISIBLE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _header_value_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    vals: List[str] = []
    # Base catalog values
    vals.extend(rng.sample(BASE_VALUES, k=min(len(BASE_VALUES), 6)))

    # Random token lists with parameters
    for _ in range(3):
        token = _rand_visible(rng, 3, 10)
        # sanitize token to common token charset
        token = "".join(c for c in token if c.isalnum() or c in "!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~")
        if not token:
            token = "tok"
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            paramv = _rand_visible(rng, 1, 8).replace(",", "").strip()
            vals.append(f"{token}; q=0.{rng.randint(0,9)}; v={paramv}")
        else:
            vals.append(token)

    # Quoted-string values with escapes
    for _ in range(2):
        s = _rand_visible(rng, 4, 24)
        s = s.replace('"', '\\"')
        vals.append(f'"{s}"')

    # Long but within typical limit used by stub (<=256)
    long_part = _rand_visible(rng, 200, 256)
    vals.append(long_part)

    return vals


def _header_name_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    names.extend(rng.sample(TOKEN_NAMES, k=min(len(TOKEN_NAMES), 5)))
    for _ in range(3):
        base = _rand_visible(rng, 3, 12)
        tok = "".join(c for c in base if c.isalpha() or c == '-')
        if not tok:
            tok = "X-Gen"
        names.append(tok[:63])
    return names


def _build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Mix of header names and values; stubs may call FUZZ_PARAM_STR for either
    names = _header_name_variants(rng)
    values = _header_value_variants(rng)

    # Ensure Connection-related values sometimes present
    conn_vals = ["keep-alive", "close"]

    # Interleave sequences: name, value, pairs, queries etc.
    seq: List[str] = []
    # Seed with a Host-like value to help HTTP header map
    host = f"example{rng.randint(1,9999)}.com"
    seq.extend(["Host", host])

    # Add Connection pair
    seq.extend(["Connection", rng.choice(conn_vals)])

    # Add Transfer-Encoding options
    seq.extend(["Transfer-Encoding", rng.choice(["chunked", "identity"])])

    # Add several random pairs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        seq.append(rng.choice(names))
        seq.append(rng.choice(values))

    # Add some standalone values that might be used for map queries
    for _ in range(3):
        seq.append(rng.choice(names))
    for _ in range(5):
        seq.append(rng.choice(values))

    # Finally some random visible strings for general consumption
    for _ in range(5):
        seq.append(_rand_visible(rng, 1, 32))

    # Serialize as length-prefixed items to let the harness split deterministically
    # Format: [count][len][data]...[len][data]
    # count: 2 bytes, len: 2 bytes, big-endian. Data is raw bytes without CRLF.
    count = min(len(seq), 200)
    out = bytearray()
    out += count.to_bytes(2, 'big')
    for s in seq[:count]:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > 512:
            b = b[:512]
        out += len(b).to_bytes(2, 'big')
        out += b

    # Keep under 4096 bytes
    return bytes(out[:4096])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _build_corpus(rng)

import random
from typing import List

def _pick_http_versions(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Common and plausible HTTP version tokens the library likely accepts.
    base = [
        "HTTP/1.0",
        "HTTP/1.1",
        "HTTP/2.0",
    ]
    # Include some less common but still valid-looking tokens to increase coverage
    extras = [
        "HTTP/0.9",   # historic
        "HTTP/2",     # some stacks accept without .0
        "HTTP/3",     # emerging
        "HTTP/1.2",   # unusual but syntactically plausible
    ]
    # Randomize order and choose a subset including duplicates to vary occurrences
    candidates = base + extras
    r.shuffle(candidates)
    # Bias to include base versions more than extras
    versions = []
    for v in candidates:
        weight = 3 if v in ("HTTP/1.0", "HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/2.0") else 1
        versions.extend([v] * weight)
    r.shuffle(versions)
    return versions


def _emit_len_prefixed_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Simple container format: count (1 byte) followed by for each string:
    # length (1 byte) and UTF-8 bytes. Length limited to 255.
    out = bytearray()
    n = min(len(strings), 50)  # keep bounded
    out.append(n)
    for s in strings[:n]:
        b = s.encode('ascii', 'strict')
        b = b[:255]
        out.append(len(b))
        out.extend(b)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Produce a small corpus buffer containing multiple valid HTTP version strings.
    Intended for FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the target stub. The stub calls set_http_version
    with c_str() and std::string overloads; we therefore provide a sequence of
    plausible versions to maximize acceptance while exploring code paths.

    Format: 1-byte count, then for each: 1-byte length + ASCII bytes.
    """
    r = random.Random(seed)

    versions = _pick_http_versions(r)

    # Add a few randomized but valid-looking variants: HTTP/{major}.{minor}
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        major = r.choice([0, 1, 2, 3])
        # typical minors 0 or 1; include others sometimes
        minor_pool = [0, 1] + ([2, 3] if r.random() < 0.3 else [])
        minor = r.choice(minor_pool)
        versions.append(f"HTTP/{major}.{minor}")

    # Deduplicate while preserving order to keep buffer compact
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for v in versions:
        if v not in seen:
            uniq.append(v)
            seen.add(v)

    # Ensure at least one canonical default if randomness removed all
    if not uniq:
        uniq = ["HTTP/1.1"]

    buf = _emit_len_prefixed_strings(uniq)
    # Keep under 4096 bytes
    return buf[:4096]
